German president meets Zardari, praises Pakistan's 'rising diplomatic profile' in dispute resolution
items.description: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier praised Pakistan’s “rising diplomatic profile in the resolution of regional and global disputes”, in a meeting with President Asif Ali Zardari in Berlin on Friday. President Zardari is currently on a three-day visit to Germany, having departed yesterday, as the two countries are set to mark the 75th anniversary of their diplomatic relations. According to a statement posted by the president’s office, the two leaders also discussed challenges related to Afghanistan. President Zardari said that while Pakistan “has no conflict with the Afghan people”, it would not allow terrorists to use Afghan soil to attack Pakistan’s citizens and violate its sovereignty. Steinmeier appreciated Pakistan for facilitating the verification of 500 Afghans “destined to be repatriated to Germany”, it said, adding that he also commended Pakistan’s humanitarian assistance to “millions of Afghans” over more than four decades. He also took a “significant interest” in the Makkah defence pact, which has been signed between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia. In response, President Zardari said the pact was aimed at “ensuring regional security and provided a security alternative to regional conflicts, and it is not directed against any specific country”. The German president expressed hope that the two countries would continue to engage with reinforced efforts in the fields of business and trade to promote “bilateral business, education collaboration and technological cooperation”. For his part, President Zardari thanked Steinmeier for his invitation and the hospitality extended to him and his delegation. President Zardari further expressed his gratitude for Steinmeier’s acknowledgement of Pakistan’s “sincere mediation role” in the conflict between the United States and Iran, the statement said. He said Pakistan viewed the resolution of conflicts through the lens of sustained dialogue and constructive negotiations, “for the sake of regional as well as global peace and stability”. During the meeting, President Zardari also stressed the need to “realise the available potential for expanding existing political, economic and defence cooperation” between Pakistan and Germany, with “greater focus on economy and trade, emerging technologies, climate resilience, skills development, people-to-people and cultural exchanges”, the statement said. The president said that Pakistan “highly values” Germany as a major European partner, and expressed admiration for German support towards women’s empowerment, social protection and human development. Pakistan was prepared for expanding bilateral cooperation beyond traditional areas into “innovative and mutually beneficial collaboration” with Germany, in the areas of scientific development, healthcare and education, vocational training and technological advancement, trade and investment, agriculture, commerce and industry, and climate resilience, through enhanced government-to-government, business-to-business and expert-level interactions, the statement further quoted President Zardari as saying. He said the visit reflected Pakistan’s “commitment to deepening its longstanding cordial, friendly relations with Germany and readiness to translate existing relations into a stronger, robust and mutually beneficial partnership through sustained constructive engagement”. President Zardari invited the German president to Pakistan, who responded that he would consider a visit “at an appropriate time”. Both presidents participated in delegation-level talks after their one-on-one meeting, according to the statement. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah and Sindh’s provincial ministers Sharjeel Memon and Jam Khan Shoro, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla and Pakistan’s Ambassador to Germany Salman Sharif were part of the Pakistani delegation. Earlier, President Zardari was given a guard of honour upon his arrival at the German Ministry of Defence, with Steinmeier also present on the occasion, the statement added. In a statement issued on Thursday, the Foreign Office (FO) said the president’s visit, scheduled for Oct 22-24, is “part of high-level exchanges between Pakistan and Germany”. During his visit, he will also hold meetings with senior leadership and business leaders, with a “particular focus on economic and trade cooperation”, the FO said. In September, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly. During the meeting, Germany appreciated Pakistan’s mediation efforts in regional conflicts, especially in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab. The two sides also agreed to “get negotiations on peace for Ukraine going”, according to the German foreign office. In June, a German delegation announced plans to bring about 30 German companies to Pakistan and link local businesses to European markets.

items.title: Port de Mostaganem : le calendrier de la spécialisation fixé
items.description: L’Algérie accélère la spécialisation du port de Mostaganem. Un mois et demi après la décision du président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, de réserver ce port exclusivement aux opérations d'importation effectuées par les entreprises et compagnies publiques, un calendrier est mis en place. Dans une note adressée aux opérateurs économiques privés du deuxième plus grand port commercial de l’ouest du pays après celui d’Oran, l’Entreprise portuaire de Mostaganem a fixé les délais pour la réorientation du trafic roulant, autre que celui des entreprises et organismes publics, au 31 octobre prochain. Toutefois, pour les navires dont les rotations ont été préalablement programmées et faisant l'objet d'engagements commerciaux déjà contractés, une période transitoire pourra être accordée jusqu’au 31 décembre prochain. Autrement dit, le port de Mostaganem ne recevra plus aucun navire en dehors de ceux destinés aux entreprises et organismes à partir du 1 er janvier 2027. Port de Mostaganem : l’activité des auto-entrepreneurs exclue Pour l'activité des auto-entrepreneurs dans le secteur du transport maritime de passagers, elle est orientée vers d'autres ports au plus tard le 31 octobre prochain, a décidé l’entreprise portuaire de Mostaganem. Ces deux mesures ont été prises dans le cadre de la « mise en œuvre des directives et des orientations de la tutelle relatives à la réorganisation des activités portuaires, et dans un souci de transférer progressivement l'activité vers d'autres ports, il a été conclu ce qui suit ». L’Algérie a lancé un vaste chantier de modernisation et de spécialisation de ses ports afin de réduire les délais d’attente des navires en rade et de réduire les délais de dédouanement et de déchargement des marchandises. L’article Port de Mostaganem : le calendrier de la spécialisation fixé est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Financer sans alourdir la dette : la méthode ANGSPE
items.description: Ligne à grande vitesse, autoroutes, aéroports : le Rapport sur l’État actionnaire 2024-2025 détaille les montages conçus par l’ANGSPE pour lever des dizaines de milliards de dirhams sans solliciter la signature de l’État. Dette portée par les régions, titrisation de redevances, émissions obligataires : ces schémas entrent dans leur phase opérationnelle. Comment bâtir une ligne à grande vitesse prolongée jusqu’à Marrakech, des RER dans trois régions et de nouveaux terminaux aéroportuaires sans alourdir la dette du Trésor ? C’est la question à laquelle l’Agence nationale de gestion stratégique des participations de l’État (ANGSPE) s’efforce de répondre, et le Rapport sur l’État actionnaire qu’elle a publié en consigne la réponse, projet après projet. La démarche, résume le document, privilégie des montages financiers innovants, qui préservent la signature de l’État et réduisent au minimum la sollicitation du Budget général. Elle accompagne les programmes liés à la Coupe d’Afrique des Nations 2025 et à la Coupe du Monde 2030, que le Royaume co-organise. Dans le communiqué accompagnant le rapport, l’Agence évoque 148,5 milliards de dirhams de besoins d’investissement couverts par des schémas de financement alternatifs structurés en 2025. Elle a par ailleurs lancé, au quatrième trimestre 2025, une étude sur le périmètre financier public, dont les conclusions sont attendues au second semestre 2026, ainsi qu’une étude sur la logistique, censée dessiner une feuille de route des synergies entre opérateurs. Le dossier ferroviaire est le plus massif. L’extension de la ligne à grande vitesse entre Kénitra et Marrakech, ainsi que les services de RER de Casablanca, Rabat et Marrakech, appellent un financement estimé à 53 milliards de dirhams. Le schéma retenu confie la levée de 48 milliards de dirhams de dette aux régions de Tanger-Tétouan-Al Hoceïma, de Fès-Meknès, de Rabat-Salé-Kénitra, de Casablanca-Settat et de Marrakech-Safi, auprès d’un consortium bancaire, l’État apportant les 5 milliards restants sous forme de fonds de dotation. L’ONCF, de son côté, participera au service de la dette d’infrastructure existante et de la nouvelle dette, une fois la ligne prolongée mise en exploitation et l’exploitation du réseau montée en charge. Les avantages mis en avant sont un impact neutre sur la dette du Trésor, un financement qui ne mobilise pas la garantie souveraine et une dette libellée en dirhams, qui écarte le risque de change. Un sondage préliminaire auprès de bailleurs de fonds a fait ressortir un intérêt potentiel supérieur à 50 milliards. Validé lors d’une réunion interministérielle le 8 janvier 2025, le schéma a débouché en mai sur un protocole d’accord entre l’État et l’ONCF. Pour les autoroutes, la mécanique est différente. ADM prévoit, à l’horizon 2032, quelque 14,5 milliards de dirhams d’investissements hors grosses réparations, dont l’autoroute continentale Rabat-Casablanca et l’achèvement du tronçon Tit Mellil-Berrechid. La moitié sera financée par la titrisation, sur vingt ans, des redevances d’occupation temporaire du domaine public que la société verse à l’État, via un fonds de placement collectif en titrisation. Les montants levés seront réinjectés dans ADM sous forme d’augmentation de capital. Le reliquat proviendra d’émissions obligataires lancées par la société elle-même, sans garantie de l’État. Titrisations et émissions seront alternées, chaque augmentation de fonds propres devant élargir la capacité d’emprunt de l’opérateur. Un protocole d’accord a été conclu le 21 mars 2025, et le futur programme obligataire constituerait une première pour la société. Le même procédé s’applique aux aéroports. L’ONDA doit financer 25 milliards de dirhams de développement des capacités, auxquels s’ajoutent 13 milliards de mise à niveau et d’acquisitions foncières. La titrisation, également sur vingt ans, des redevances d’occupation du domaine public dégagera 5 milliards, versés en fonds de dotation. L’Office compte ensuite sur 25 milliards de dettes non garanties par l’État, par voie d’obligations, de crédits bancaires et de concours de banques multilatérales, ainsi que sur 8 milliards d’autofinancement. Le protocole d’accord correspondant a été signé le 24 juillet 2025, sous la présidence du Chef du Gouvernement. D’autres opérations, plus modestes, suivent la même logique. Nador West Med a émis en 2024 un premier emprunt obligataire de 1,2 milliard de dirhams, sur quinze ans et remboursable in fine, sans garantie de l’État ni aucune autre sûreté ; un second, de 500 millions, est en cours, pour un total de 1,7 milliard. Chez Barid Al-Maghrib, le réseau d’agences est cédé à sa filiale Al Barid Bank, laquelle augmente son capital d’un montant équivalent, ce qui a donné lieu à une première opération d’environ 530 millions de dirhams en 2024 et à un dividende de 250 millions versé par BAM, contre 100 millions un an plus tôt. Le schéma de la SOREAD-2M relève d’une autre veine, celle du sauvetage. La société affichait une situation nette de moins 1 123 millions de dirhams fin 2024, pour un capital d’environ 359 millions. La conversion en capital des avances d’associés et une augmentation de capital en numéraire, qui solde au passage sa dette fiscale envers l’État, ont été réalisées, selon le rapport, pour 1,1 milliard de dirhams. Reste l’apport d’actifs immobiliers à un OPCI dédié, dont les dividendes seront titrisés, les biens étant loués à l’État, qui les mettra à la disposition de la SOREAD-2M ; l’effet cumulé des trois premiers leviers sur la situation nette est estimé à 1 397 millions. Dans l’énergie, la refonte de la convention tripartite entre l’État, l’ONEE et MASEN vise explicitement à supprimer l’appui financier de l’État à l’équilibre des projets de MASEN et à mettre fin au recours à sa garantie. L’ONEE devient l’acheteur unique et prend en charge le futur écart lié aux centrales solaires à concentration, ce qui appelle un schéma de refonte capitalistique permettant son entrée au capital de MASEN. L’État, lui, assume l’écart antérieur à l’entrée en vigueur de la convention, valorisé à 3 milliards de dirhams. The post Financer sans alourdir la dette : la méthode ANGSPE appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ethique et qualité : l’ANAQ-Sup et l’OFNAC s’allient pour assainir l’enseignement supérieur
items.description: L'Autorité nationale d'Assurance Qualité de l'Enseignement supérieur (ANAQ-Sup) et l'Office national de Lutte contre la Corruption (OFNAC) ont signé ce vendredi 23 octobre 2026 un accord-cadre de partenariat stratégique. Objectif : faire de l'intégrité un critère à part entière de la qualité des universités, écoles doctorales et centres de recherche du Sénégal. La cérémonie était présidée conjointement par Moustapha Ka, président de l'OFNAC, et le professeur Massamba Diouf, secrétaire exécutif de l'ANAQ-Sup. Les deux institutions parlent d'une alliance inédite, alignée sur le référentiel Sénégal Vision 2050. Leur conviction commune : l'excellence académique ne va pas sans gouvernance irréprochable. Moustapha Ka a donné le ton avec la formule suivante : « Un diplôme sans éthique est un pouvoir sans boussole. » Il a poursuivi : « Par la Qualité, nous élevons le Savoir ; par l'Intégrité, nous honorons la République. » Le professeur Diouf a insisté sur la méthode. « L'intégrité ne doit pas être envisagée uniquement sous l'angle de la sanction, mais comme une culture et une responsabilité partagée », a-t-il rappelé, estimant que la qualité de l'enseignement supérieur « ne saurait être pleinement garantie sans une gouvernance fondée sur l'éthique, l'intégrité, la transparence et la redevabilité ». Quatre chantiers prévus -Évaluation : intégrer des critères de gouvernance de l'intégrité, de prévention des risques de corruption et de transparence dans les manuels d'évaluation de l'ANAQ-Sup. -Formation : développer des modules sur la déontologie, l'intégrité scientifique et la prévention du plagiat. -Académie de l'Intégrité : l'ANAQ-Sup apportera un appui technique à cette initiative de l'OFNAC, en vue d'accréditer les qualifications qui y seront délivrées. -Plateforme de l'intégrité académique et scientifique : un observatoire produira données, indicateurs et cartographies des risques pour éclairer les décisions publiques. Un suivi par feuilles de route Un Comité mixte de pilotage validera des feuilles de route annuelles. La première priorisera l'identification des risques institutionnels, le renforcement des guides d'évaluation et la formation des acteurs académiques. O.B.N

items.title: Russia says Ukraine, US talks ‘planned’ for Abu Dhabi
items.description: Talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States are planned to resume in November in the United Arab Emirates, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Friday. Russia indicated its readiness to resume the talks, which have been at a standstill since the beginning of the year, following a meeting this week in Saint Petersburg between President Vladimir Putin and US special envoy Steve Witkoff. The next round of talks towards ending the Ukraine war, which is grinding through its fifth year, are “planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi”, and “will take place in a trilateral format”, Peskov told reporters. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the plan to meet in November in a post on X. “Now we all need to focus on making these meetings happen –- together with America, Europe, and all our partners,” he said Friday. The announcement came amid intensified diplomatic efforts by US President Donald Trump’s administration. Witkoff met on Tuesday with Zelensky and European leaders in Oslo, before meeting with Putin on Wednesday. Following the meetings, both Kyiv and Moscow voiced their readiness to resume direct talks mediated by Washington. Russia, which launched its full-scale offensive against Ukraine in February 2022, has suggested talks could take place “around November 10”. Zelensky has called for the discussions to happen “as soon as possible”. In a televised interview aired late Thursday, Putin said that any trilateral talks would focus on the security arrangements of a final peace deal and not a “short” truce. items.title: Dubréka : le DGA de l’Institut supérieur des Arts Mory Kanté tué dans un accident
items.description: Le directeur général adjoint chargé des études de l’Institut supérieur des Arts Mory Kanté de Dubréka, Amadou Bah, est décédé ce vendredi 23 octobre 2026, à la suite d’un accident de la circulation survenu à Kénendé, sur l’axe Dubréka–Kagbelen. Sa disparition suscite une vive émotion au sein de l’établissement et parmi ses collègues et collaborateurs. Selon les informations recueillies auprès de ses proches collaborateurs, le drame s’est produit alors qu’il se rendait à Conakry pour assister à des obsèques. Il aurait emprunté un tricycle qui, d’après les premiers témoignages, serait entré en collision avec un cortège militaire en route vers Boffa. Grièvement blessé, Amadou Bah aurait notamment souffert de fractures et d’une hémorragie interne. Transporté à l’hôpital préfectoral de Dubréka, il a finalement succombé à ses blessures. Joint par l’intermédiaire de ses collaborateurs, le chargé de communication de l’Institut a indiqué que le défunt avait passé une partie de la matinée dans les locaux de l’établissement. Il y avait échangé avec plusieurs responsables avant de prendre la route pour assister aux obsèques. « Au cours du chemin, ils ont été frôlés par un cortège militaire. Il avait beaucoup saigné. C’est de là qu’il a été transporté à l’hôpital préfectoral de Dubréka, où il a trouvé la mort », a-t-il rapporté. La nouvelle du décès d’Amadou Bah a pris de court ses collaborateurs, dont certains l’avaient rencontré quelques heures seulement avant le drame. Le directeur de la bibliothèque de l’Institut raconte avoir échangé avec lui dans la matinée, dans un lieu où ils avaient l’habitude de se retrouver autour d’un café, en dehors des heures de cours. Au cours de leur conversation, Amadou Bah lui avait notamment parlé d’un rendez-vous prévu à Sonfonia aux environs de 11 heures. Informé plus tard de l’accident par M. Diallo, secrétaire général de la cellule syndicale, ce collaborateur s’est rendu à l’hôpital préfectoral de Dubréka. Sur place, il dit avoir constaté la gravité des blessures du responsable universitaire. Il explique également avoir attendu des nouvelles de l’équipe médicale, dans l’espoir qu’une évacuation vers Conakry puisse être organisée. Malgré les efforts du personnel soignant, Amadou Bah n’a toutefois pas survécu. Sa disparition constitue une lourde perte pour l’Institut supérieur des Arts Mory Kanté de Dubréka, où il occupait les fonctions de directeur général adjoint chargé des études.

items.title: Ghana unveils world Armwrestling championship squad, appeals for travel support
items.description: The Ghana Armwrestling Federation has unveiled a formidable squad for the upcoming World Armwrestling Championship in New Delhi, India, while appealing to corporate Ghana, government institutions, philanthropists and sports enthusiasts to support the team’s travel and participation. The squad, comprising some of the country’s most accomplished Armwrestlers, is expected to fly Ghana’s flag at the global competition as the team targets medals and seeks to consolidate the country’s growing reputation as a force in international armwrestling. Leading the contingent are world-class performers Mabel Yeboah-60kg, Blessed Abeka Nunoo – 65kg and Grace Minta – 89kg, who have distinguished themselves through their performances at international competitions. They are joined by Florence Boakye – 110+kg, Afia Kumah – 110+kg and Comfort Dunyo – 60kg, who are masters in the women’s category. The men’s contingent includes Edward Asamoah Yamoah, Haruna Tahiru, Godwin Sackey, Daniel Acquah, Charles Osei Asibey Jr., Henry Otoo and Asinu Dodzie, all expected to bring their strength, experience and competitive spirit to the championship. Ghana’s participation is particularly significant given the country’s impressive progress in the sport over the years, with its athletes making their mark at continental and world competitions. The national team has consistently demonstrated its potential to challenge the world’s best, earning recognition for Ghana on the international sporting stage. However, despite the team’s ambition and preparations, securing the necessary financial resources to facilitate the trip remains a major concern. The Federation is therefore appealing to corporate institutions, government agencies, sports-loving individuals and other stakeholders to support the squad’s travel and participation. The appeal comes at a crucial time, with the Federation seeking to ensure that financial constraints do not prevent the selected athletes from representing their country at the prestigious championship. Support from the private sector and other well-meaning Ghanaians would provide an important boost to the team’s campaign while offering sponsors an opportunity to associate their brands with a sport that continues to deliver results and enhance Ghana’s international sporting profile. The Ghana Armwrestling Federation has, over the years, built a reputation for developing athletes capable of competing at the highest level, while creating opportunities for talent development, employment and national pride. The Federation is hopeful that the latest appeal will attract the necessary support to enable the team to travel to India and compete against the world’s best armwrestlers. The 2026 World Armwrestling Championship is scheduled for India from October 26 to November 7, 2026.

items.title: Coastal Road: ‘I’m local champion; you’re pretender’ — Gov Diri replies Duke
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri has hit back at former Cross River State governor and Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) presidential candidate Donald Duke, calling him a “jester and a pretender” after Duke’s remarks about the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. In a recent interview on Arise Television, the PRP candidate called governor Diri a “local champion” while arguing that the coastal road project was not feasible because of its cost and Bayelsa State’s terrain. Diri had earlier rejected Duke’s claim that building the highway through Bayelsa was not feasible, adding that the ex-governor is “not abreast of current developments in road construction and infrastructure” in Bayelsa. Reacting to Diri’s comment, Duke said: “The governor of Bayelsa, if he did say so, I don’t know the fellow, but if he did say so, I think he’s just being a local champion.” One week after Duke’s comment, Governor Diri, in a video which has now gone viral, fired back at the PRP candidate, saying he’s a local champion elected to defend his people. “Yes, I’m a local champion, because that is where I was raised. I am elected to defend the local people. I am elected to champion their cause. But Donald Duke, let me ask you, you were on seat when Bakassi was ceeded out of Nigeria. “You were the sitting governor of Cross River state. Because you are not a local champion, you did nothing about it. I believe that you are more of a jester and a pretender,” he said. Diri also questioned Duke’s political standing in his own ward, and said the dispute was about his people and the region, not simply a personal disagreement. “Donald Duke, I am not one who takes up people, I am not one of those who insult people; I don’t insult leaders; I don’t insult elders but what you have done is not just about me, it is about my environment, it is about my people.” The governor further defended the region’s development potential, saying Bayelsa and other coastal communities should not be defined by their difficult terrain. “Donald Duke, I am not that fellow, I am the sitting governor of Bayelsa state. All of us from this region, particularly from Bayelsa state, do not accept the narrative that your state cannot be developed. We have a very rich ancestry, our terrain is one of the best if we develop it and we are prepared to take our destiny into our hands.” Diri also thanked the President for supporting the coastal road, describing it as an opportunity to address poverty and the dehumanisation of coastal communities. The post Coastal Road: ‘I’m local champion; you’re pretender’ — Gov Diri replies Duke appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Newsfile to discuss Obuasi SHTS abuse case, GH₵49m SA evacuation, World Cup visa scandal
items.description: This Saturday on Newsfile: three scandals, new revelations, unanswered questions. When complaints are made, and institutions fail to act; when millions of cedis are spent, but records remain disputed, and when money allegedly connected to a visa scandal is returned, what does accountability really mean? This Saturday on Newsfile, we examine three controversies raising difficult questions about public trust, institutional responsibility and the search for the truth. The Obuasi Senior High Technical School sexual-abuse scandal continues to deepen, with the number of reported complainants rising to 19. Two education directors have been asked to step aside to facilitate investigations, while allegations that 38 teachers were targeted for transfers have raised concerns about possible retaliation against whistleblowers. The NDC, which initially directed the accused headmaster to withdraw from its constituency chairmanship contest, reversed that decision in the name of natural justice and the presumption of innocence, before directing him to step aside again. Meanwhile, the headmaster has reportedly sued Manasseh Azure Awuni and Multimedia Group Limited for GH¢2 million in defamation damages. But as the allegations are investigated, who is protecting the students? Does the presumption of innocence prevent authorities from taking precautionary measures to safeguard children and preserve public confidence? If complaints were brought to the attention of school and education officials months earlier, who knew, what action did they take, and will anyone be held accountable for failing to act? With civil society organisations calling for a sex offenders’ register, mandatory background checks and stronger school safeguarding systems, how can Ghana protect children without unfairly branding people whose guilt has not been established? And what changes are needed to ensure that no school becomes the scene of similar allegations? From the safety of schoolchildren, we turn to the management of public funds. The GH¢49.72 million spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa remains the subject of a heated dispute between the government and the Minority. Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa insists that every cedi has been accounted for. The NPP Minority, however, says its examination of the records has uncovered discrepancies involving passenger manifests, allowances and supporting documentation, raising questions about GH¢16.4 million in expenditure. JoyNews ‘ independent examination has also identified errors in passenger records, including impossible dates of birth, prompting Ghana’s High Commission in Pretoria to acknowledge mistakes affecting 15 records. The mission attributes those inaccuracies to passport expiry dates being entered in place of dates of birth, insisting that the errors do not establish financial loss. But the controversy has now moved beyond clerical mistakes to the cost of charter flights. The Minority is questioning the reported US$750,000 price tag for each of three flights and demanding original contracts, airline invoices and procurement records. Were the flights procured competitively? What services were covered by the reported charges, and were any intermediaries involved? Can the Ministry demonstrate not merely that money was paid, but that the services were delivered at a reasonable cost? The government says the expenditure is fully accounted for, while the Minority insists that questions remain. With a special audit reportedly requested, will an independent examination finally reconcile the figures and establish whether the discrepancies are administrative errors, weaknesses in record-keeping or evidence of more serious irregularities? And in the unfolding World Cup visa scandal, a reported US$26,000 payment to police on behalf of suspended National Sports Authority Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah has introduced another twist. The payment is said to be part of US$56,000 allegedly received as commission in connection with visa arrangements. Ampofo Ankrah denies wrongdoing, and the reported repayment is not proof of criminal liability. But who made the payment, under whose instructions, and for what purpose? Was it a refund to an applicant, a recovery of disputed money or part of an arrangement to settle the matter privately? And what happened to the investigation into alleged abuse of public office and financial irregularities involving public institutions and private intermediaries? Should the OSP become involved, and how should its mandate be coordinated with the CID’s ongoing investigative role? More importantly, can returning money extinguish criminal liability if an offence has been committed, or must investigators still establish how the money was obtained, who benefited, and whether public office was used for private gain? Is Ghana investigating a suspected criminal enterprise, or will the matter ultimately be treated as a financial dispute resolved by repayment? Three stories, one fundamental test: whether institutions can be trusted to protect the vulnerable, account for public money and investigate allegations without fear or favour. From the classrooms of Obuasi to the evacuation accounts and the World Cup visa controversy, the public deserves more than denials, accusations and promises of investigations. It deserves answers supported by evidence, fair processes and accountability where wrongdoing is established. This Saturday, join Samson Lardy Anyenini and the Newsfile panel as we interrogate the latest revelations, examine the competing claims and ask the questions that matter. Newsfile airs live on the JoyNews channel on digital satellite channels 421 on DSTV and 144 on GoTV, and streams on JoyNews’ Facebook or YouTube channels on Saturdays from 9 am to noon. Viewers can also follow the discussion by tuning in to Joy 99.7 FM or Luv 99.5 FM on the radio or stream the discussion live on either Google or Apple Podcasts. When it’s Saturday, it’s Newsfile! Newsfile is your most authoritative news analysis programme.

items.title: Govt raises high-speed diesel rate by Rs1.91 per litre; petrol price unchanged at Rs377.71
items.description: The government on Friday raised the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.91 per litre, leaving the petrol rate unchanged at Rs377.71. Following the revision, HSD will cost Rs393.66 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable from Oct 24 (Saturday) to Oct 26 (Monday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
items.description: Seven people have been killed in an attack on a funeral in central Jordan, officials have said. At least 34 others were injured as gunmen opened fire on a church in Hmoud, in the Karak governorate on Friday. The unidentified gunmen are reported to have arrived in a car, entered the church and opened fire before fleeing. No-one has admitted carrying out the attack. In a news conference, Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said authorities were working to apprehend the perpetrators which he described as a “group of extremists”. Jordan’s King Abdullah II, said the authorities would “confront the terrorist act that targeted Karak with the harshest penalties”. “Whoever imagines that the bullets of treachery can divide the ranks of Jordanians will fail in his endeavour before our steadfastness and unity,” the king added in a post on X. Dozens of people had been inside the church for the funeral when the shooting began, Khaled Burqan, one of the mourners, told Jordan’s al-Mamlaka state-run TV. He said two attackers armed with a rifle and a pistol had been firing at the mourners for several minutes. Al-Faraya added that the incident was “painful and horrific” and “unparalleled in the history of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan,” during his news conference. Public service television station al-Mamlaka has reported the king arrived in Karak on Friday evening “to check on the condition of the injured”. Initial reports indicated seven people had been killed in the attack. A government spokesperson later said six people had died, before officials again revised the death toll to seven. CCTV footage, verified by the BBC, appears to shows three gunmen making their way from a road toward the church. Two of the attackers are seen making their way on to what appears to be a vehicle entrance to the church grounds, before retreating briefly and returning with a third man. All three appear to be armed with handguns. Separate footage believed to be from the aftermath of the attack appears to show several dead and wounded bodies on the ground amid some chaotic scenes. There was a heavy security presence at the entrance to a hospital treating people injured in the incident in Karak, amid an atmosphere charged with anger among residents of the governorate, particularly the families of those injured and killed. Karak has a sizeable Christian community in the majority-Muslim Jordan. Such violence is rare in the country, but deadly attacks have been carried out in the past. Lebanon’s President Joseph Aoun, a Christian head of state, said the “heinous terrorist attack” on the church “violated the sanctity of death and funeral mourners, contradicts all religious and humanitarian values,” according to Lebanese media.

items.title: ATU seeks support to address infrastructure gaps
items.description: Accra Technical University (ATU) is seeking financial support to address infrastructure gaps and improve the delivery of technical education. The university plans to launch an endowment fund on October 23 to mobilise resources for infrastructure development and other institutional needs. The initiative comes as ATU marks 10 years since its transition from a polytechnic to a technical university in 2016. Speaking on the university’s development priorities, Finance Director Frank Owusu Boateng said the fund would help address some of the resource constraints facing the institution. “We hope that we will get some seed money, which will indeed grow to help us get some of the infrastructure things that we currently lack,” he said. Technical education and job creation Mr Boateng also emphasised the need for graduates of technical universities to apply their practical skills beyond seeking conventional employment. He said the hands-on training students receive should equip them to establish businesses and create jobs for others. “The idea is that it works both ways. You either get a job out there or, with the better skills you have acquired, the hands-on skills you have acquired, you should be able to create your own job, and even employ others to work for you,” he said. His comments highlight the importance of equipping graduates with practical competencies that can support entrepreneurship and contribute to employment creation. Debate marks 10 years of transition ATU’s infrastructure and development needs featured in discussions during its 10th anniversary inter-university debate. The contest examined the motion: “This House Believes That Transitioning Polytechnics to Technical Universities Has Helped the Course of Technical Education in Ghana.” The debate provided an opportunity for students to assess the impact of the transition on technical education and discuss its contribution to skills development. ATU Debate Society coach Michael Koranteng expressed excitement over the university’s performance in the competition, describing the outcome as a proud moment for the team. “As we had exhibited today, ATU came in tops, and as a coach, I am particularly grateful and very excited to be part of the success story,” he said. Mr Koranteng also noted that debate offers students opportunities to develop communication and argumentation skills while building relationships that support their personal and academic growth.

items.title: GTEC summons technical university leaders, TUTAG for talks over strike
items.description: The Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) has invited management of all technical universities and national leaders of the Technical University Teachers’ Association of Ghana (TUTAG) to a meeting to address concerns raised by the association amid its ongoing industrial action. The meeting is scheduled for Wednesday, October 28, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. at the Ahmed Jinapor Room of the GTEC Conference Hall. In an invitation letter issued on October 21, the Commission said the meeting would bring together vice-chancellors, finance directors, registrars and union representatives to discuss TUTAG’s concerns and explore ways to address the issues raised. “This meeting aims to bring together management, financial leadership, and union representatives to foster an open dialogue, address current challenges, and discuss TUTAG’s concerns,” GTEC said. The Commission stressed the importance of the discussions to maintaining institutional harmony and promoting academic excellence, urging the invited stakeholders to attend and contribute to the deliberations. “Given the importance of this policy discussion to institutional harmony and academic excellence, your personal attendance and expertise will be highly valued,” the invitation stated. GTEC has also asked the invitees to confirm the number of representatives expected to attend to facilitate logistical arrangements. The meeting comes as efforts continue to resolve the concerns underpinning TUTAG’s industrial action, which has affected technical universities. Meanwhile, TUTAG’s national executive is expected to convene an Extraordinary Congress on Monday, October 26, to deliberate on proposals and a position presented by the Vice-Chancellors of Technical Universities Ghana (VCTU-G) towards a possible suspension of the strike.

items.title: L’Onu doit négocier le virage pour éviter le naufrage (Par Oumar NDIAYE)
items.description: Le revers essuyé par tous les sept candidats au poste de Secrétaire général de l’Organisation des Nations unies (Onu) lors du sixième Straw poll (vote indicatif), le 16 novembre dernier, semble faire vivre à cette institution des travers sans précédent. Même s’il est vrai que cette situation n’est pas si différente de celle de 1996 avec la nomination de Koffi Annan en remplacement de l’Egyptien Boutros Ghali, elle contraste de la nomination du Portugais Antonio Guterres en 2016. L’ancien Premier ministre du Portugal avait dominé tous les votes indicatifs. La succession d’Antonio Guterres qui va terminer son mandat en décembre prochain est ainsi relancée avec peut-être d’autres candidats. Pourtant, l’actuelle short-list était assez intéressante, avec des candidats venus de l’Amérique latine et des profils qui connaissent bien l’organisation de l’intérieur, ou l’ancien président sénégalais Macky Sall qui peut se prévaloir d’une expérience de quatre décennies de vie publique. Ce désaveu relance ainsi le débat sur l’avenir d’une organisation qui, depuis quelques années, traverse une crise structurelle et existentielle. Comme rappelé dans deux précédentes chroniques, la première écrite il y a cinq ans, intitulée « Sous Biden, le multilatéralisme devra se réinventer », et la deuxième l’année dernière, « Les coups de boutoir et l’échappatoire du multilatéralisme », le multilatéralisme malgré tout a aidé beaucoup de pays, dans toutes les régions du monde, à combler des vides de l’État et apporter soutiens et subsides. Mais aujourd’hui, dans leur marche, certaines organisations multilatérales, surtout l’Onu, commencent à subir le poids de l’âge. Ainsi, les péripéties qui accompagnent la désignation du prochain Secrétaire général des Nations unies, loin d’être une tragédie, symbolisent les divisions et divergences auxquelles cette institution fait face depuis plusieurs décennies. Héritière de la Société des Nations (Sdn) née en 1918 des cendres fumantes de la Première Guerre mondiale, l’Onu a repris les mêmes idéaux et fondamentaux de sa devancière. Portée par le président américain, Woodrod Wilson, un des noms les plus cités dans la théorie de l’Idéalisme des Relations internationales, la Sdn se voulait une organisation internationale tournée vers la paix et la sécurité internationale. Mais l’âge d’or de l’Idéalisme n’a pas trop duré parce que le monde, comme le décrivent les penseurs de la théorie du Réalisme, est marqué par les rapports de force entre les États et aussi une observation froide de la réalité des Relations internationales. C’est ce postulat qui a présidé aux premières années de l’Onu après sa création en 1945 avec ainsi des places occupées par les forts que sont les membres permanents du Conseil de sécurité : États-Unis, Chine, Russie, France et Grande-Bretagne. Mais le monde post-Seconde Guerre mondiale a beaucoup évolué avec un changement radical de réalité. Longtemps à la périphérie de la gouvernance mondiale, les pays du « Global South » commencent aujourd’hui à peser de leurs poids dans la marche du monde. Alors qu’auparavant, avec les instruments du multilatéralisme comme les Nations unies ou les institutions de Breton Woods, les grandes décisions du monde se prenaient à Washington ou à New York, ou bien dans leurs annexes européennes. Ainsi, de par leur âge, des institutions comme l’Organisation des Nations unies créées sur les braises de la Seconde Guerre mondiale n’épousent plus les aspirations et ambitions surtout des pays du « South Global » qui sentent toujours la domination du camp occidental. C’est dans ce contexte que se joue la succession d’Antonio Guterres qui est un moment phare dans l’évolution de l’Onu. L’Organisation se trouve ainsi dans un vrai tournant. Elle doit ainsi bien négocier ce virage pour ainsi éviter un naufrage, qui sera lourd de conséquences pour le multilatéralisme… oumar.ndiaye@lesoleil.sn

items.title: U-17 WWC: Flamingos beat North Korea 3-1 to reach knockout stage
items.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Nigeria’s Flamingos have advanced to the knockout stage of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup after defeating defending champions North Korea 3-1 in their final Group B match. The Flamingos secured the victory at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Salé, Morocco on Friday. Nigeria went into the encounter needing a win to guarantee their progress after losing to Poland in their second match, having opened their campaign with a 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico. Akeem Busari’s side rose to the occasion, with Oluwakemi Adegbuyi opening the scoring in the 15th minute. Oluebube Umejiaku extended Nigeria’s lead in the 38th minute, beating North Korea’s high defensive line before finishing past the goalkeeper. Kanyisola Yusuf then put the Flamingos firmly in control with a third goal early in 56th minutes North Korea pulled one back through a penalty in the 82nd minutes, but Nigeria held firm defensively to preserve their two-goal advantage and secure the victory. The result saw Nigeria finish second in Group B behind North Korea, who claimed top spot on goals scored. Poland ended the group stage in third place despite finishing level on points with the top two teams. items.title: Don’t sacrifice NDC’s 2028 ambition for internal elections – Majority Leader
items.description: Majority Leader and Builsa North MP James Agalga has cautioned members of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) against allowing internal rivalry ahead of the party’s constituency elections to undermine its preparations for the 2028 general elections. In an appeal to party members ahead of Saturday’s, October 24, constituency polls, Mr Agalga urged candidates and their supporters to prioritise the party’s collective interest over individual ambitions. He stressed that although the elections were an important part of building the party’s grassroots leadership, members must exercise restraint in their campaigns and avoid personal attacks that could create divisions. “We all have a stake in the 2028 journey. Let us not undermine that future in our quest to serve the Party today,” he said. Mr Agalga further called for peaceful engagements throughout the electoral process, urging party members to demonstrate unity, love and respect in their interactions. He said the process should be free from insults and character assassination, adding that the outcome should leave the NDC stronger and more united. The Majority Leader also wished all aspirants well, expressing hope that the elections would be conducted peacefully and that the best candidates would emerge victorious.

items.title: Chinese naval hospital ship arrives in Tema for a seven-day medical mission
items.description: The Chinese People’s Liberation Army Navy hospital ship, AUSPICIOUS ARK (Hull 868), has arrived at Tema port for a seven-day humanitarian medical mission and friendly visit to Ghana under Mission Harmony 2026. The vessel arrived on Friday, October 23, 2026, marking its first reported visit to the country. The mission is expected to provide medical services to the public and strengthen professional exchanges between Ghanaian and Chinese military medical personnel. The Flag Officer Commanding the Eastern Naval Command, Commodore Raymond Kyaano, who was the Guest of Honour at the arrival ceremony, welcomed the ship and its crew on behalf of the Chief of the Defence Staff, Lieutenant General William Agyapong, and the Ghana Armed Forces. He described the visit as an important opportunity to advance humanitarian assistance, deepen medical cooperation and promote the health and well-being of Ghanaians. Commodore Kyaano also commended the visiting crew for their commitment to humanitarian service, noting that the provision of specialised medical care demonstrated the values of compassion, service and international solidarity. The Mission Commander and Commanding Officer of AUSPICIOUS ARK , Rear Admiral Guan Bailin, expressed confidence that the visit would expand medical exchanges and strengthen professional relationships between the medical teams of the two countries. He said the engagements would facilitate the sharing of clinical knowledge and experience, particularly in naval medicine, specialised healthcare delivery and emergency medical response. The mission is also expected to allow personnel from both countries to learn from each other’s healthcare practices and approaches to humanitarian assistance. As part of the programme, the ship will provide medical consultations and other healthcare services to members of the public using its onboard medical facilities. The vessel is equipped with specialised departments and facilities, including laboratory services, a dental clinic, gynaecology, ophthalmology, stomatology, surgical theatres and inpatient wards. Beyond the services to be provided aboard the ship, medical outreach teams are expected to visit the China-Ghana Friendship Hospital and a military camp to conduct consultations, academic exchanges and professional engagements with Ghanaian healthcare personnel. The seven-day mission is scheduled to end on Friday, October 30, 2026. The opening ceremony brought together representatives from the Ghana Armed Forces, the Ministry of Health, the Ghana Health Service, the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority and other institutions, alongside the visiting Chinese naval delegation.

items.title: Mahama joins Ethiopian PM to inaugurate Megech Dam project
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has joined Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali to inaugurate the Megech Irrigation Development Project in Gondar, Ethiopia, as part of his official visit to the country. President Mahama arrived in the historic city on Friday at the invitation of Dr Abiy Ahmed Ali, ahead of the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa, scheduled to take place in Bahir Dar. Shortly after arriving at Gondar Airport, the Ghanaian President joined the Prime Minister to switch on the dam-and-reservoir project, which is expected to boost agricultural production and improve water supply in the region. The project, which was initiated 18 years ago, stalled until Dr Abiy revived it three years ago and oversaw its completion. Covering 870 hectares and with a storage capacity of 185 million cubic metres, the Megech Dam is expected to support irrigation across 17,000 hectares of farmland, improving agricultural productivity and strengthening food security. The facility will also provide a reliable supply of clean drinking water to Gondar and its surrounding satellite towns. President Mahama commended the Ethiopian government and people for their resilience and commitment to completing the project, describing it as a major development expected to benefit generations to come. On Saturday, President Mahama is expected to travel to Bahir Dar to chair the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa. The forum will bring together African leaders, policymakers and security experts to deliberate on key peace, governance and security challenges facing the continent.

items.title: TUTAG to hold extraordinary congress on proposed strike suspension on October 26
items.description: The Technical University Teachers’ Association of Ghana (TUTAG) will hold an Extraordinary Congress on Monday, October 26, 2026, to consider proposals from the Vice-Chancellors of Technical Universities Ghana (VCTU-G) towards suspending its ongoing industrial action. The planned congress follows an engagement between the leadership of TUTAG and VCTU-G to resolve the outstanding issues that triggered the strike. In a statement issued on Friday, October 23, 2026, the association expressed appreciation to the vice-chancellors for their concern and commitment to finding an amicable resolution to the dispute. TUTAG reaffirmed its commitment to constructive dialogue and collaboration to achieve a settlement acceptable to both parties. Ahead of the congress, the association has urged members of VCTU-G to engage the chairpersons of their respective TUTAG local chapters and persuade them to support the proposed suspension of the industrial action. “We therefore consider it particularly important that the proposed engagements with the Local Chapter Chairmen take place ahead of Congress, to help build the necessary consensus towards a favourable outcome,” the statement said. Read also: Technical University Vice-Chancellors appeal to TUTAG to call off strike The association said the congress would give its national executive an opportunity to present and deliberate on the proposals and position outlined by VCTU-G before members decide on the way forward. TUTAG also reiterated its appreciation for the vice-chancellors’ engagement and expressed optimism about continued collaboration to resolve the outstanding issues. The industrial action by university administrators continues to disrupt administrative services at public universities as efforts to resolve the dispute proceed.

items.title: Tinubu’s Kaduna rally won’t save him in 2027 — Makinde campaign
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organization (MDPCO) has dismissed President Bola Tinubu’s planned 2027 campaign flag-off in Kaduna State, declaring that insecurity, economic hardship and alleged marginalisation of the North would cost him re-election. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Ihediwa, the organisation said Saturday’s rally would not erase public anger over Tinubu’s record, insisting that the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate, Engr. Seyi Makinde, was poised to defeat him. The campaign organisation challenged Tinubu to justify his administration’s record in the North, recalling his 2022 campaign promise to eliminate bandits and kidnappers troubling Kaduna and other parts of the region. “Since President Tinubu decided to flag off his 2027 Presidential campaign in Kaduna, the political headquarters of the North, we challenge him to explain what the region has gained from his incompetent and nepotic administration beyond a bumper harvest of bloodshed, crushing economic hardship, broken promises and shattered public trust,” Ihediwa said. The MDPCO claimed that at least 13,000 people had been killed in northern Nigeria since Tinubu assumed office in 2023, while an estimated 3.7 million had been displaced. It also accused the administration of protecting APC campaign billboards while communities remained vulnerable to attacks, and alleged that the North had been sidelined in strategic federal appointments. “Under Tinubu, political advertisements appear better protected than human lives,” the organisation said. The organisation said Tinubu’s assurance that Northerners would never regret voting for him had been undermined by worsening insecurity and economic hardship, arguing that the region deserved more than campaign promises. It urged Nigerians to embrace Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA Agenda, expressing confidence that public discontent would translate into an electoral setback for the APC in 2027. The post Tinubu’s Kaduna rally won’t save him in 2027 — Makinde campaign appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le silence des femmes n’est pas coupable (Par Matel BOCOUM)
items.description: Les hommes ont haussé le ton pour dénoncer le silence des mouvements féminins à la suite du meurtre du sexagénaire Cheikh Oumar Ndiaye par sa deuxième épouse. Mais c’est ignorer que le silence ne rime pas forcément avec indifférence. Celui des femmes, loin d’être coupable, traduit, quelque part, une sidération face à un acte qui dépasse l’entendement. Au nom des principes universels des droits humains, des femmes ont, elles aussi, condamné cette violence létale. Qu’elle soit commise par un homme ou une femme, elles ne peuvent la cautionner. Une vie humaine demeure sacrée. Nul n’a le droit de tuer. Elles ont été nombreuses à s’indigner en apprenant qu’une jeune femme de 20 ans, enceinte, aurait mortellement poignardé son époux pendant son sommeil, à la suite d’un différend familial. Selon des informations rapportées par la presse, elle lui reprochait notamment d’avoir frappé son fils, né d’une précédente union. La nouvelle a provoqué un profond émoi. Les cœurs ont été meurtris. Les statistiques criminelles montrent que les femmes restent très minoritaires parmi les auteurs d’homicides et de crimes violents. À l’échelle mondiale, les hommes sont largement surreprésentés parmi les auteurs de violences létales. Mais cette réalité statistique ne saurait conduire à nier les violences commises par des femmes, notamment dans le cadre familial. Il est souvent souligné que certaines formes de violence sont moins visibles : violences verbales, psychologiques, émotionnelles ou relationnelles, brimades, humiliations, pressions morales ou harcèlement. On les impute souvent à la gent féminine. Dans certains foyers, les conflits conjugaux, les tensions liées à la polygamie ou encore les difficultés de cohabitation vont jusqu’à créer des situations de grande violence. Si des hommes dénoncent aujourd’hui ce qu’ils considèrent comme des indignations à géométrie variable, il faut reconnaître qu’ils ne sont pas les seuls. Des féministes se sont inscrites dans la même dynamique. La sociologue Nathalie Heinich, dans son ouvrage, « Etats de femme : l’identité féminine dans la fiction occidentale », met notamment en garde contre une conception d’une justice fondée sur l’appartenance à une catégorie plutôt que sur l’examen des faits. Elle considère qu’un individu ne devrait pas être jugé en fonction de son sexe, mais de ses actes. Faire du sexe de l’auteur un critère déterminant de culpabilité reviendrait à renoncer, selon ses explications, à l’un des principes fondamentaux de la justice : la responsabilité individuelle. Elle invite à éviter des lectures trop simplistes des relations humaines et à s’interroger concrètement sur les causes concrètes qui conduisent à la violence : histoire personnelle, environnement familial, éducation, conflits conjugaux, précarité, emprise, traumatismes ou encore exposition à certains contenus numériques. Sous nos cieux, le meurtre de Cheikh Oumar Ndiaye a également suscité la réaction d’hommes qui estiment qu’il est temps de parler de certaines violences qu’ils disent subir dans la sphère privée. Tout en reconnaissant que les femmes sont statistiquement minoritaires parmi les auteurs d’homicides volontaires, ils évoquent des violences physiques non mortelles, mais aussi verbales, psychologiques et émotionnelles. Ces situations existent et méritent d’être entendues. Les reconnaître ne signifie nullement mettre sur le même plan toutes les formes de violences ni effacer les réalités documentées des violences faites aux femmes. Il s’agit plutôt de rappeler qu’aucune violence ne devient acceptable parce qu’elle est commise par une femme. Dans l’espace familial, les conflits peuvent parfois dégénérer. Tensions conjugales, rivalités, jalousie, conflits liés à la polygamie ou difficultés de cohabitation peuvent donner lieu à des comportements agressifs. Mais il convient de ne pas transformer ces réalités en accusations générales contre les femmes. Le silence des femmes face au meurtre d’un homme ne peut pas être interprété comme une approbation. Et la dénonciation des violences subies par certains hommes ne doit pas être perçue comme une attaque contre les combats féministes. L’humanité prime sur toute autre considération. matel.bocoum@lesoleil.sn

items.title: US could strike Iran this weekend, envoy says
items.description: The United States could strike Iran as soon as this weekend, a US envoy said Friday, after mounting threats by both Washington and Israel. “Could there be a strike this weekend? Absolutely,” Tom Barrack, the US ambassador to Turkey and point man on Syria who does not have a direct role on Iran, told podcast host Mario Nawfal. President Donald Trump “is very clear. He’s open and available and accessible to a deal and we’ve been at the table for months and months and months,” Barrack said in an interview as he visited the Gulf. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces elections Tuesday, has in recent days repeatedly vowed to topple the clerical state in Iran, following two major bombing campaigns against it since last year. Trump has also signalled an openness to resuming strikes after a long deadlock in diplomacy, although he earlier said it would not happen before US congressional elections on November 3. Barrack, in remarks that contradict Netanyahu, said the US was not looking to topple the Islamic republic, a sworn enemy of the United States and Israel since a 1979 revolution toppled the pro-Western shah. “If you keep threatening the world, our allies, the Gulf, there will be a consequence. The consequence won’t be regime change,” Barrack said. “The United States — the president of the United States — has said he’s not interested in regime change,” he added. “The problem with regime change always is, what’s the day-two scenario?” The post US could strike Iran this weekend, envoy says appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: UN sounds alarm on besieged Yemen city Taiz
items.description: Time is running out to get aid into Taiz, besieged by pro-Iran Houthi fighters who are preventing supplies from reaching Yemen's third-largest city, the United Nations said Friday. Houthi fighters have encircled Taiz since early October, blocking the road that links it to Aden, interim capital of the Saudi-backed, internationally-recognised government. "Safe, sustained and unimpeded humanitarian access is urgently needed so that essential supplies and life-saving assistance can reach people in need," said the UN humanitarian agency OCHA.

items.title: Welcome to the Valley of Pain
items.description: This week could go down as the worst in the history of cybersecurity. On Wednesday, news emerged about two major vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language used by 70 percent of websites, which prompted governments, hospitals, and companies around the world to take digital services offline as a precaution. There have already been millions of attempts to exploit these weaknesses. But the PHP vulnerabilities were just the most attention-grabbing in a series of alarming revelations. Security flaws in, or successful hacks of, several major software products and platforms—including some used by Netflix, PayPal, Walmart, and other big names—were announced that same day. Yesterday, Quest Diagnostics, which runs lab tests for a third of American adults each year, disclosed that it, too, had been breached. When I asked Sam Rubin, a senior vice president at the cybersecurity firm Palo Alto Networks, about the potential fallout from yet another hack—this one of the cloud platform Railway, which is used by Intuit and MGM Resorts, among others—he paused. “I didn’t see that one,” Rubin said. “It’s been quite a busy week.” [ Read: ‘If anything happens to this guy … everyone is screwed’ ] Yet what’s most alarming about the past few days is that by next year, this stretch of incidents—which some security experts are calling “Black October”—may be remembered as normal, or even tame. “It’s going to feel like, over and over and over again, we’re finding more and more bugs in very critical pieces of software,” Matthew Prince, the CEO of the internet infrastructure and security company Cloudflare, told me. “This story, which feels unique and fresh right now—in a few months, it’s going to feel like we get one of these every week.” Prince said he knows of still more vulnerabilities that will be announced in the near future. For the next year or two, if not longer, the internet is going to feel a bit touch and go, and more dangerous than we’ve come to expect. “It’s going to feel like the sky is falling” for a while, Prince said. There’s a decades-long backlog of bugs in software written without much review or scrutiny—which was more or less fine so long as there was a very small number of skilled hackers. Over the past two decades, companies, governments, and individuals have been lulled into a false sense of security: Most people don’t think twice about punching credit-card numbers into the website of a local restaurant or gift shop, or forking over a home address and phone number in just about any customer survey. But the internet was always a dangerous place. We’re just waking up from a trance. AI agents can now be deployed as a cheap and near-infinite hacker army. In just the past couple of months, Rubin said, open-source models—which can be downloaded for free and used without restrictions—have become very good at finding vulnerabilities and automating attacks. In turn, the amount of malicious cyber activity has spiked. More websites will be defaced, more personal information will be stolen, and ransomware will proliferate. Rubin told me that the internet is entering a “valley of pain.” When I posed the concern that this is the new normal to Adam Meyers, a senior vice president at the cybersecurity company CrowdStrike, he told me, “I think it’s going to get a lot worse, actually.” Consider, for instance, another set of vulnerabilities disclosed this week, to the program Node.js. This software, which executes JavaScript code for dynamic webpages, is widely used by Fortune 500 companies, as well as in programs developed with AI. “These are the things the web runs on,” Meyers said. Because of how the platform is used, compromising just one software product that uses Node.js could infect tens of thousands of other organizations, Rubin said, in what is known as a “supply-chain attack.” And the skill threshold for launching cyberattacks has become almost absurdly low: CrowdStrike tied a spate of cyberattacks on South Korean banks late last month to a 26-year-old in China. “After he got access to all the data, he turned around and asked AI, ‘How do I monetize this? Where can I sell this?’” Meyers told me. He “didn’t know what he was doing.” Meyers said CrowdStrike is detecting “a new agentic adversary”—that is, an AI-powered hacking operation—“every two hours.” Navigating this will require rapid and tremendous coordination from basically every sector. For instance, the vulnerabilities in PHP were discovered months ago by a consortium of AI and cybersecurity firms. Then, “very quietly, for the last several months, we and other industry partners worked to effectively put in place protections,” Prince said—basically, temporary shields until the weaknesses could be fully addressed. But “not everybody uses CloudFlare, and not everybody is quick to patch their software.” Some of the cybersecurity experts I’ve spoken with are optimistic about AI: Eventually, they say, AI will be used to find and address many of the major cybersecurity flaws, and the internet will become much safer overall. But before then, we may be stuck in a terrible limbo. “This is going to last as long as it takes to rewrite and secure the billions of lines of code that have always had these vulnerabilities,” Alex Stamos, the chief information-security officer at the AI company Cognition and a former chief security officer at Facebook, told me. And even as cybersecurity experts rush to leverage AI to save the internet, the technology is introducing plenty of new problems. All vibe-coded apps, for starters, are very likely to contain security flaws. And at a time when people need to be more vigilant about their digital hygiene, multiple cybersecurity experts brought up the widespread adoption of AI assistants with more than a hint of scorn; as Rubin put it: “Our peers are using Muse and giving it carte blanche to use your credit card.” The internet is becoming a wilder place, and the path to secure it may require, in essence, a sort of pruning. “You’ll likely see more companies take services off the internet when they don’t need to be there,” depreciating old webpages and forms so they can’t be targeted, Dan Guido, the CEO of the cybersecurity firm Trail of Bits, told me. Individuals might be encouraged to delete unused browser extensions, he added, so that there are “fewer pieces of software that can access your data.” People in general need to be “more discerning of the companies they work with,” Stamos said, and “you’re just not gonna be able to assume every site you use is secure.” That Pokémon trading-card website, fantasy-sports platform, or birding forum you use could be hacked for a password you’ve reused elsewhere, or a credit-card number, or worse. Other advice I heard: Don’t host your own email client instead of Gmail. Don’t host your own file system at home instead of using the cloud. Google and Dropbox have the resources to defend against an onslaught of AI hacks, and you don’t. If, eventually, we do find and shore up all of the cybersecurity vulnerabilities out there, the result could be a more open web, where anybody can use widely available AI tools to run security checks at any time and you’ll feel safer sharing your personal information again. But another possibility is an even more centralized internet, where only services and websites developed by large software providers are deemed trustworthy and reliable. The internet needs new walls to defend against AI-powered attacks. But in turn, we might also feel walled in.

items.title: Kumasi Traders Federation Chairman enstooled as Nerebehi Chief
items.description: Chairman of the Federation of Kumasi Traders Association, Nana Kwarteng Apegyabie Prempeh II, has been enstooled as the new Chief of Nerebehi, a community, in the Atwima Nwabiagya South municipality of the Ashanti Region. Known popularly as Nana Akwasi Prempeh, he was nominated as the new chief on July 31, 2026, after receiving the unanimous support of the community’s kingmakers. He was formally and traditionally enstooled on Thursday, October 22, 2026, after swearing an oath of allegiance to the Bantamahene, Baffour Owusu Amankwatia IV, at the Bantama Palace. The ceremony brought together hundreds of residents, chiefs, and family members from Nerebehi, who thronged the palace to solidarise with the new chief. Nana Kwarteng Apegyabie Prempeh II will hold the title of Bantamahene Apakanhene and oversee the traditional council of Nerebehi and twelve surrounding communities. Addressing the new chief, the Bantamahene urged him to unite his people to accelerate development in the community. “Unity and a shared sense of purpose are critical for Nerebehi to achieve greater development,” he admonished. The community welcomed the new chief’s nomination, describing him as a unifying leader who is committed to local development. Speaking after his enstoolment, Nana Kwarteng Apegyabie Prempeh II pledged to lead with humility, discharge his duties assiduously, and remain servile wherever he is requested by the Bantamahene. He expressed gratitude to the Bantamahene, his elders, the Nerebehi community, and its traditional leaders for their support. He also urged his subjects to rally behind him to foster peace and unity as well as accelerate development in the community.
