items.title: Delta govt approves N4bn to empower 1500 indigenes
items.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi & Ochuko Akuopha The Delta State Government has approved N4 billion to empower 15,000 indigent residents to support small businesses and entrepreneurship. The initiative is part of efforts to ease economic hardship across the state. The State Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information, Mr Charles Aniagwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists after the State Executive Council meeting presided over by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori at Government House, Asaba. The Commissioner who was accompanied by the Chief Press Secretary to the Governor, Sir Festus Ahon, said beneficiaries will be drawn from the 25 local government areas under an initiative designed to improve livelihoods and strengthen the purchasing power of vulnerable residents. Aniagwu said the intervention would be implemented through the Delta State Social Investment Programme in the coming weeks, adding that the governor had directed that the selection process be guided by clear eligibility criteria. According to him, priority will be given to indigent persons who already operate small businesses, those seeking to establish micro-enterprises and vulnerable residents who require financial support to improve their circumstances. He said the grant was intended to help existing businesses overcome economic challenges, provide start-up capital for aspiring entrepreneurs and enable beneficiaries to meet pressing needs. The commissioner explained that the initiative was part of the government’s efforts to ensure that the benefits of ongoing economic reforms translated into tangible improvements in the lives of ordinary Deltans. items.title: Kompany hospitalised after collapsing at Bayern training ground
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany has reportedly been taken to hospital after collapsing at the club’s training ground on Friday, amid concerns over a viral infection that has affected his health in recent days. According to Sky Sports Germany, the 40-year-old Belgian received medical attention before being taken by ambulance to a hospital in Munich. A rescue helicopter was also seen landing at Bayern’s training complex at Säbener Straße. Reports said Kompany had been battling a viral infection that caused significant discomfort, including problems with his legs and difficulties climbing stairs. German newspaper Bild also reported that the illness had aggravated problems involving old scar tissue. The former Manchester City captain had experienced health concerns before Bayern’s 6-1 Bundesliga victory over RB Leipzig last weekend, when he reportedly spent periods of the match seated in the dugout. He subsequently missed training and the pre-match press conference ahead of Bayern’s Champions League meeting with Arsenal on Wednesday, leaving assistant coach Aaron Danks to address the media. Danks said Kompany had been advised to rest while recovering, although he acknowledged that persuading the manager to take time away from his duties was difficult. “Getting Vince to rest is a challenge,” Danks said. Kompany recovered sufficiently to take charge of Bayern’s 2-2 draw with Arsenal at the Allianz Arena. After the match, he admitted that he had continued working despite the illness. “I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn’t listen to my body,” he said. The latest reports said Kompany was in a stable condition, although the precise circumstances surrounding the reported collapse remained unclear. Bayern had not issued a detailed official medical update at the time of reporting. The German champions are scheduled to face Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday, with Kompany’s availability for the fixture uncertain. Assistant coach Danks could take charge if the Belgian requires further time to recover. The post Kompany hospitalised after collapsing at Bayern training ground appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kedougou : un site d’orpaillage clandestin démantelé, 25 motopompes saisies
items.description: Les forces de sécurité ont démantelé, mercredi 22 octobre 2026, un site d’orpaillage clandestin situé à cinq kilomètres du village de Tenkoto, dans la région de Kédougou. L’opération a permis la saisie de plusieurs équipements utilisés pour l’exploitation aurifère. Les éléments de la brigade de proximité de Sabodala, en poste à Tenkoto, appuyés par l’Escadron de surveillance et d’intervention (ESI) de Kédougou, ont procédé au démantèlement d’un site d’orpaillage clandestin situé à cinq kilomètres du village de Tenkoto. Menée le mercredi 22 octobre 2026, l’opération a permis aux forces de sécurité de saisir un important lot de matériel, comprenant 25 motopompes, six motocyclettes, cinq machines dites « cracheurs », deux tricycles motorisés et 70 bassines en plastique. L’enquête se poursuit afin de déterminer les circonstances de cette activité clandestine et d’identifier les personnes impliquées.

items.title: Télécommunications : Des accords de roaming pour faciliter les communications au sein de l’UEMOA
items.description: La signature des accords bilatéraux d’itinérance entre les acteurs concernés des États membres de l’Union économique et monétaire ouest-africaine (UEMOA) marque une nouvelle étape dans la coopération numérique régionale. La cérémonie s’est tenue le vendredi 23 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, en marge de la deuxième session du Comité des régulateurs nationaux du numérique (CRNN). Faciliter les communications au-delà des frontières et améliorer l’expérience des usagers. C’est l’objectif poursuivi par les accords bilatéraux de roaming. Ils s’inscrivent dans la dynamique de renforcement de l’intégration numérique au sein de l’espace communautaire de l’UEMOA. Ces accords visent à répondre aux besoins des populations qui se déplacent d’un pays à l’autre, notamment pour maintenir le contact avec leurs proches, poursuivre leurs activités professionnelles et accéder aux services numériques. Pour les autorités, leur portée ne doit pas se limiter à la signature des documents, mais se traduire par des améliorations concrètes dans les conditions d’utilisation des services de télécommunications. La ministre de la Transition digitale, des Postes et des Communications électroniques, Dr Aminata Zerbo/Sabané, a salué l’engagement des parties signataires ainsi que le travail des autorités de régulation, des experts et des opérateurs ayant contribué à l’aboutissement du processus. « Les accords bilatéraux de roaming que vous venez de signer donnent une traduction concrète à notre volonté de faciliter les communications entre nos pays », a déclaré Dr Aminata Zerbo/Sabané. Pour elle, la pertinence de ces engagements devra être appréciée à travers l’expérience quotidienne des usagers . « Les accords signés aujourd’hui constituent une étape dont l’utilité devra se mesurer à l’expérience des usagers », a-t-elle souligné. « Pour nos populations, le roaming ne constitue pas simplement un mécanisme technique ou réglementaire », Wendlassida Patrice Compaoré La ministre a également insisté sur la nécessité d’assurer un suivi rigoureux des engagements pris. « J’invite les parties concernées à poursuivre leur coordination pour assurer leur mise en œuvre conformément aux dispositions convenues », a-t-elle indiqué, appelant à une meilleure information des usagers sur les conditions d’utilisation des services et les démarches à suivre en cas de difficulté. Au-delà de la signature, l’effectivité des accords constitue un défi pour les autorités de régulation et les opérateurs de télécommunications. Le suivi des engagements, la transparence des conditions d’utilisation et le traitement rapide des difficultés rencontrées par les usagers figurent parmi les exigences mises en avant lors de la cérémonie. Le Secrétaire exécutif de l’Autorité de régulation des communications électroniques et des postes (ARCEP) du Burkina Faso, Wendlassida Patrice Compaoré, a également souligné l’importance de cette étape. Dans son mot de bienvenue, il a rappelé que le roaming répond à une préoccupation concrète des populations. « Pour nos populations, le roaming ne constitue pas simplement un mécanisme technique ou réglementaire », a-t-il déclaré. Il a expliqué que ces accords doivent permettre aux citoyens de rester connectés lorsqu’ils franchissent une frontière, de communiquer avec leurs proches, de poursuivre leurs activités professionnelles et d’accéder aux services numériques dans des conditions claires, transparentes et accessibles. Pour le responsable de l’ARCEP, l’essentiel réside dans les résultats concrets de ces engagements. « C’est pourquoi la véritable portée de ces accords se mesurera non seulement à leur signature, mais surtout à leur mise en œuvre effective et aux bénéfices que les usagers pourront concrètement en tirer » , a-t-il affirmé. La signature des accords bilatéraux de roaming ouvre ainsi une nouvelle phase, celle de leur mise en œuvre et de leur suivi. La capacité des parties prenantes à respecter les engagements pris et à résoudre les difficultés éventuelles sera déterminante pour renforcer l’intégration numérique et faciliter la mobilité des populations au sein de l’espace UEMOA. Faso7 L’article Télécommunications : Des accords de roaming pour faciliter les communications au sein de l’UEMOA est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

Turkey says renewed attack on Iran would expand conflict, diplomacy only way
items.description: ISTANBUL, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan cautioned on Friday against any renewed attack on Iran, saying such a move would exacerbate tensions and further expand the conflict there, adding that diplomacy and dialogue were the only way to end the war. Fidan met his counterparts from Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Germany, France, Britain and Italy in Istanbul to discuss developments in the Iran war, attacks on Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi militants, and Russia's war in Ukraine.

items.title: Zelenskiy says Ukrainian, Russian and US negotiators to meet in early November in Abu Dhabi
items.description: By Andrea Shalal and Olena Harmash WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Friday that peace negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States had agreed to meet at a technical level in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, adding that he hoped a meeting of the countries' leaders would follow.

items.title: Second batch of GAF recruits report for basic military training
items.description: The second batch of recruits of the Ghana Armed Forces (GAF) have officially reported to various training centres to commence Basic Military Training on Friday, October 23, 2026. The recruits have reported to the Army Recruit Training School, Air Force Recruit Training School, Navy Recruit Training School, Armour Training School and Army Special Operations Training School. They are expected to undergo six months of basic military training aimed at instilling discipline, professionalism and the core values of the Ghana Armed Forces. The training programme will cover key military subjects, including field craft, first aid, weapon handling, drill, map reading and physical training, among others. The programme is designed to equip the recruits with the requisite skills needed to uphold the standards, traditions and values of the Armed Forces. The commencement of the training marks an important step in the recruits’ journey towards becoming professional soldiers of the Ghana Armed Forces.

items.title: REMA 2026 : Les clés pour convertir les followers en acteurs de la carrière d’un artiste
items.description: À l'occasion de la 9e édition des Rencontres musicales africaines (REMA), des panels ont été organisés autour du thème « Followers, passer de passif à actif », décliné en plusieurs sous-thèmes, au Centre culturel du Faso. La transformation des abonnés des réseaux sociaux en une communauté engagée au service de la carrière des artistes était au cœur des échanges, ce vendredi 23 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Du 22 au 24 octobre 2026, Ouagadougou vibre au rythme des REMA 2026. « Les followers comme une force économique » : c'est autour de cette problématique que se tient cette 9e édition. Dans une ambiance interactive, les panélistes ont communiqué sur les enjeux de l'engagement numérique dans l'industrie musicale, au Centre culturel du Faso. Pour Nidhal Chemingui, panéliste, le simple fait de suivre un artiste constitue déjà une forme d'engagement Au-delà du nombre d'abonnés, la question est désormais de savoir comment transformer une audience virtuelle en une communauté qui écoute les œuvres, participe aux concerts et contribue à la promotion des artistes. Pour Nidhal Chemingui, panéliste, le simple fait de suivre un artiste constitue déjà une forme d'engagement. « Il n'y a pas de followers passifs : ils se sont déjà engagés dans une action en venant vers l'artiste », a-t-elle estimé. L'enjeu consiste donc à trouver les moyens de renforcer cet intérêt initial et d'amener les abonnés à interagir davantage avec les artistes qu'ils suivent. Pour le journaliste et panéliste Marius Diessongo, il est essentiel pour un artiste de disposer de followers, mais surtout de maintenir leur intérêt dans la durée Dans cette dynamique, la création d'une communauté autour de l'artiste apparaît comme un levier important. Pour le journaliste et panéliste Marius Diessongo, il est essentiel pour un artiste de disposer de followers, mais surtout de maintenir leur intérêt dans la durée. Pour y parvenir, il recommande de construire une communauté avec laquelle l'artiste peut partager son quotidien, discuter et échanger. À l'heure où les artistes investissent des plateformes comme TikTok, Instagram, Facebook et X, les échanges ont également mis en lumière la responsabilité des artistes dans la gestion de leur présence sur les plateformes numériques. Le public… Pour Will Be Black, artiste musicien et participant au panel, il est nécessaire de s'entourer de personnes compétentes et de développer une stratégie de communication digitale adaptée. « Il incombe à l'artiste de s'entourer de personnes adéquates, d'être présent sur l'espace digital et de trouver les voies et moyens pour que les followers, les fans parlent de lui partout et en tout temps », a-t-il retenu des discussions. Il faut noter que les REMA se poursuivent jusqu'au 24 octobre 2026, au Centre culturel du Faso. Les mélomanes et les passionnés de musique sont attendus ce soir à partir de 20 h pour les showcases. Lire aussi : REMA 2026 : La musique burkinabè, porte-voix de la cohésion sociale Nadège KINDA Minute.bf

items.title: Khartoum courts UN-backed relief to stave off truce pressure; Tasis govt heedful after health minister’s angry exit; Abyei strike tests Juba ties; Drones hit RSF, military’s seats of power; RSF pushes in Kurmuk, military wins Geisan ground
items.description: Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter here . From Khartoum and Nyala, to a gold mine in South Kordofan, a town in West Kordofan and a power station in White Nile, drones tore through Sudan this week, killing hundreds and destroying homes, livelihoods and critical infrastructure. Both sides traded blame, and each pointed to neighbors it said let the drones through. Some strikes went unclaimed, but silence from the military over its attack on the disputed Abyei region didn’t stop Juba from summoning Sudan’s ambassador on the same day to warn of a “dangerous development” in a border territory already straining relations between the two countries. Khartoum weighed in days later, with a Foreign Ministry statement denying the military was involved. The strike on the RSF-held Naam market in Abyei set fuel depots burning. The fires were still consuming the area as the death toll exceeded 150 and thousands were displaced, and residents took to the streets in protest, activists and Abyei administration sources said. In the Security Council, in Geneva and among mediators on Sudan, the warnings this week over the drone war and the humanitarian toll sounded much as they have for months, and they still amount to little beyond adding pressure on the warring parties to stop the fighting. But Khartoum won’t concede an end to RSF territorial control before a truce can take hold, and won’t see the paramilitary group at the table in any political process on the country’s future. So instead of committing to a broader settlement, it is now trying to show it can deliver on humanitarian issues, betting that progress on aid deliveries and civilian protection will blunt international criticism, former and current Sudanese officials and sources close to the Transitional Sovereignty Council told Mada Masr. Hence the letters to Western capitals over the week and the talks with the United Nations on internationally monitored aid deliveries, which allow Khartoum to appear willing to engage without participating on terms it rejects, former officials said. Any plan, however, has to keep aid under the authority of state institutions, they added. In western Sudan, the RSF’s parallel administration is trying to hold on to the very recognition Khartoum is trying to deny it, but its own infighting is getting in the way. Tasis’s Cabinet is trying to take oversight of medical aid away from a health minister who had protested for months over interference by the RSF and influential figures looking to monopolize medical supplies. He left for Nairobi in protest last week, and a government already reeling from recent defections is treading carefully, wary of another exit that would further damage its image as a viable administration before aid organizations. In Blue Nile State, the push and pull on the battlefield goes on. The RSF and its ally, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North led by Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, tried to take two of the military’s bases in Kurmuk locality, part of the network protecting the state capital of Damazin, though accounts of how it ended conflict. The military, meanwhile, gained ground in neighboring Geisan locality, taking two areas that a former military officer said could help check the RSF’s new advances in Wad al-Mahi locality. *** Military drone strike on Abyei market draws protest from Juba Caption: Undersecretary of the South Sudanese Foreign Ministry Agnes Adlino Orifa Oswaha and Sudan’s ambassador to Juba, Essam Karar, discuss the attack on the Naam market in Abyei, October 19. Courtesy: The South Sudanese Foreign Ministry via Facebook. A drone strike carried out by the military on the Naam market in northern Abyei — the disputed border territory between South Sudan and Sudan’s RSF-held West Kordofan — on Monday has stoked new diplomatic friction between Khartoum and Juba. The death toll from the strike has risen to more than 150, as efforts to recover bodies were initially hampered by fires spreading from fuel depots hit in the attack, a South Sudanese source in the office of Yohana Akol Ngor , the caretaker information minister in the Abyei administration, told Mada Masr. Around 8,000 people have also been displaced, the source said. Juba responded by summoning Sudan’s ambassador to Juba, Essam Karar , on the same day to protest the attack, a source at the South Sudanese Foreign Ministry told Mada Masr. The ministry’s Undersecretary Agnes Adlino Orifa Oswaha told the ambassador that the strike was a dangerous development that called for urgent measures to prevent its recurrence and protect civilians, the source said. The Sudanese military itself issued no immediate response. Days after the attack, in the early hours of Friday, Sudan’s Foreign Ministry issued a statement expressing regret over the casualties and categorically denying the military’s responsibility for it, calling the strike “similar to the crimes the rebel militia continues to commit.” Yet a senior source in the Sudanese Armed Forces’ General Staff said the military had targeted fuel trucks arriving from South Sudan that he said were bound for the RSF. The source denied that civilians had been targeted, claiming that those killed were RSF members and that the strikes hit the group’s trucks at locations “outside the market, rather than the market as a whole.” On Tuesday, residents and civil society activists took to the streets in Abyei to protest the bombing and demand protection for civilians, a source in local civil society organizations told Mada Masr. Bulabek Deng Kual, the chief of the Ngok Dinka, one of the two main tribal groups in the area alongside the Messiria , also urged the United Nations, the African Union, the Intergovernmental Authority on Development and the South Sudanese government to act to protect residents, the source said. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres condemned the attack in a statement issued late Tuesday. The toll, he said, is expected to rise as the UN interim security force in the region continues to verify casualties, with many missing. “I call on the governments of South Sudan and Sudan to take all steps possible to help prevent further attacks and uphold Abyei’s demilitarized status,” he added. The strike hit a market that serves as an economic lifeline for communities in the region. Cross-border trade has made the Naam market a major source of income for the Ngok Dinka and Messiria , a source in the Messiria previously told Mada Masr. The market is under RSF control, as is the rest of West Kordofan, and the group has used it to secure fuel supplies and as a staging and mobilization point for South Sudanese fighters recruited to fight alongside its forces, the source said. The market sits in a region where the political dispute has never been settled. The 2005 Comprehensive Peace Agreement established special arrangements for Abyei and called for a referendum on whether the territory should belong to Sudan or South Sudan. The vote has never happened, and South Sudan’s independence in 2011 left the question of sovereignty unresolved. The UN Interim Security Force for Abyei remains responsible for security in the area. That unresolved status has long made Abyei vulnerable to tensions between the two countries, particularly as people, goods and armed groups move across a border that remains politically contested. The dispute has been reignited as South Sudan prepares for its first general election in December. Juba’s decision in June to include Abyei among its electoral constituencies angered Khartoum, prompting regional diplomatic efforts to contain the fallout and keep the dispute from undermining the electoral process. Meanwhile, Sudan has begun reorganizing its own approach to the issue. In early October, Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair and military chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan appointed retired Major General Al-Khair Abu Mureidat to lead the Sudanese side of the joint oversight committee for Abyei, replacing Lieutenant General of Police Hamed Manan. Abu Mureidat told Mada Masr that the committee would return to the agreements signed by the two countries and “pursue a peaceful resolution to differences.” He nevertheless reaffirmed Khartoum’s position that Abyei belongs to Sudan. On October 15, Foreign Minister Mohie Eddin Salem chaired the first meeting of Sudan’s national negotiating team on Abyei, which was established under a decision issued by Burhan in late September. In remarks broadcast on Sudan’s national radio, Salem said the team would seek to restart talks with South Sudan on the region’s administration, security arrangements and final status. The negotiations are to be based on the 2005 Abyei protocol and the 2011 Agreement on Temporary Arrangements for the Administration and Security of the Abyei Area. *** RSF drones kill dozens at gold mine market in South Kordofan Aftermath of an RSF drone attack on the market at the Bajon gold mine in Gadir, eastern South Kordofan, October 16. Courtesy: The Sudanese Mineral Resources Company via Facebook. At least 45 people were killed and dozens injured when RSF drones hit the market at the Bajon gold mine in the military-held Gadir locality, eastern South Kordofan, on October 16, a medical source in the area told Mada Masr. It was the second time in less than a week that drones had struck the mine. An earlier attack on October 10 caused no deaths, two miners in the area told Mada Masr. The latest strike, however, hit a market where miners, traders and other workers depend on gold production for their livelihood. The attack destroyed processing facilities and nearby shops, putting hundreds at risk of losing their livelihoods in an area with few economic alternatives and limited relief services, they added. The two miners blamed the RSF for the attack, as did the Sudanese Mineral Resources Company, which buys gold from traditional miners in Bajon. In a statement issued on Saturday, the company said preliminary assessments showed damage to four major complexes housing gold extraction and processing mills but did not mention any casualties. It said fewer workers were likely to have been present because the attack took place on a Friday. But the market was busy when the drones hit, according to a source close to miners and the families of those killed. The drones struck the main market and water-based processing mills in successive attacks, setting off fires that spread to nearby shops and storage areas. Miners, laborers, shopkeepers and people providing services to the mining trade were among those caught in the strikes, the source said. The death toll became clearer as rescuers pulled victims from beneath the rubble, according to the medical source who is in the local casualty-counting committees in Gadir. Reaching the site was difficult, while disrupted communications networks slowed both evacuations and the exchange of information between rescue teams, they said. The full toll remains uncertain. No final list of casualties has been compiled, and a detailed breakdown by age or gender is not yet available, the medical source said. Residents and local relief groups have been doing much of the work of transporting the wounded to medical facilities, he added. Using makeshift means , they transported the injured to health facilities in Gadir, Liri and Talody, where shortages of medical supplies and limited capacity have made treatment difficult. Those needing emergency surgery or transfer to better-equipped hospitals face particular risks, the source said. Families are also struggling to establish what happened to their relatives. Local volunteers have been burying the dead and trying to identify them, but many of the mine workers came from other parts of Sudan, he added. Due to unreliable communication networks, contacting families and verifying reports of deaths, injuries and missing people has been difficult. Traditional mining sites attract workers from across Sudan and support a wider network of traders, transporters, equipment suppliers and businesses providing food and other essentials. Damage to facilities at Bajon threatens the livelihoods of people who depend on this trade, even if they were not directly involved in mining, the source added. A South Kordofan government official informed of developments on the ground told Mada Masr that the attack took place in an area where mining operations, trade routes and contested zones of military control overlap, drawing traditional gold production into the war’s economic and logistical networks . In his view, the RSF regard mining areas as strategically important because of their links to gold revenues and local trade. Production at Bajon could remain disrupted until the damage to its processing facilities is assessed and repaired. Machinery, power supplies and other operating infrastructure may all affect how soon work can resume, a source informed of the Sudanese Mineral Resources Company ’s operations told Mada Masr. The company is coordinating with technical teams and regional offices to assess the damage and determine its implications for production and gold deliveries in the state, an official in its environment and safety department said. *** Dayslong m ilitary drone strikes on Nyala Nyala, the capital of South Darfur State, was pounded by military drones this week in one of the largest air campaigns against the seat of the RSF-led parallel administration in months. The raids began on Friday, October 16, with strikes a military source described as among the most intense in months. They hit several sites, including the livestock market north of the city, where the source said RSF armored vehicles were targeted, and the Cinema neighborhood, where a training camp the RSF had set up inside Nyala University was hit. The Tasis alliance said in a statement that the strike on the busy market killed at least 30 civilians and injured 43 others, claiming the drone was launched from the Egyptian military base in East Oweinat. Meanwhile, the military said its air force carried out “concentrated” strikes that day on RSF command centers and the positions of what it called the group’s mercenaries in Nyala, killing dozens of them and destroying the command centers. After a brief pause, the raids resumed on Sunday and continued until Wednesday. The strikes hit ammunition depots and the headquarters of RSF field commanders, the military source and a resident of the city told Mada Masr. Civilians were among those killed and injured, they added. *** RSF drones hit Khartoum, airport area bears the brunt Mere days after military drones began raiding the RSF’s de facto capital, the paramilitary group’s drones struck Khartoum in waves, concentrated around the international airport and extending across other parts of the capital’s south and east. Three eyewitnesses told Mada Masr that explosions began in eastern Khartoum at around 6:30 am on Monday and continued in five waves throughout the day and evening. Military anti-aircraft fire could also be heard, they said. Two drones fell in the Burri and Imtidad Nasser neighborhoods east of the airport in central Khartoum, killing four people, including three children from the same family, an official told Mada Masr. Their mother sustained serious injuries and was taken to the hospital, while parts of the family’s house were destroyed. The drones had crossed eastern and northern Gezira State before some were seen flying over Khartoum’s East Nile locality toward the eastern part of the capital, a military source told Mada Masr. Monitoring systems suggested they were most likely launched from sites in the South Sudanese town of Rank and the Ethiopian cities of Bahir Dar in the Amhara region, and Asosa in Benishangul-Gumuz , the source said. On Wednesday, ground defenses shot down three drones, one in Bagir in southern Khartoum and two in East Nile, the military source added. The area around Khartoum International Airport was among the main targets of the attacks. The airport, which had served as a major RSF stronghold during most of the war and witnessed some of the capital’s fiercest battles, reopened in February for the first time since the war began in April 2023. In May, just a week after international flights resumed, drone strikes hit the airport. Khartoum publicly attributed the attack to Ethiopia, setting off a diplomatic rift that has since widened. While the May attack damaged airport facilities and the runway, an engineer working at the airport told Mada Masr that this week’s attacks caused no damage. Amgad Farid, Burhan’s political advisor, said on Monday that the airport continues to operate normally despite what he described as “terrorist attacks launched from some neighboring countries.” *** RSF drone strike on White Nile’s Tendelti substation cuts power to North Kordofan cities Two missiles from an RSF strategic drone set the power substation in Tendelti, White Nile State, ablaze in the early hours of Tuesday, knocking it out of service, a military source told Mada Masr. The station feeds the main power line to North Kordofan State, so the strike cut electricity to three cities, Um Rawaba, Rahad and t he state capital of Obeid, along with a number of villages and towns, an activist in Um Rawaba told Mada Masr. Power resumed to North Kordofan on Wednesday evening once the state electricity distribution company had repaired the grid , an official at the company said. Tendelti itself remains in total darkness, and restoring its transformer and power supply could take until the middle of next week, he added. The blackout is disrupting other services, with water and bread shortages emerging in Tendelti, the activist said, warning that conditions will deteriorate if the outage drags on. *** Dozens killed in a military drone attack on West Kordofan town A military drone strike on the town of Dibab in West Kordofan State killed 84 people and wounded others on Sunday, a medical source in the area told Mada Masr, as conflicting accounts emerged over whether the attack hit civilians traveling or RSF fighters being moved toward the frontlines. Three former West Kordofan government employees living in Muglad and aligned with the RSF told Mada Masr that the drones struck trucks carrying civilians traveling around the area. However, an activist from the region said the strikes hit RSF fighters who had been mobilized and were on their way to Nyala before heading to the frontlines. The men had been gathered under the supervision of RSF commander Adam Gareh and assembled in buildings previously used by the group’s security service, the activist said. They were later transferred in two transport trucks accompanied by several combat vehicles. Videos circulated by activists on social media showed moments before the trucks were hit, along with the names of those killed. The Tasis alliance, meanwhile, described the gathering as civilian. In a statement , it said those targeted had congregated after attending a funeral and were preparing to travel by truck. According to the alliance, the drone first struck the truck, then returned to bomb people who had gathered to assist the wounded, leaving 80 dead and many more injured, including women and children. Tasis added that the same drone struck Muglad, where it said a missile landed near a girls’ school and wounded at least two people. The Emergency Lawyers rights group said military drones struck Muglad market on Saturday and resumed attacks on Dibab, killing dozens, including civilians. The strikes took place as the military stepped up preparations for large-scale ground operations from North Kordofan into northern West Kordofan. Air raids on RSF positions have intensified across the region in recent weeks. Throughout the past week, the air force carried out intensive strikes on West Kordofan’s Khawi, Abu Edam, Nayem, Um Maraheek, Udayyah and Babanusa, targeting RSF capabilities and supply lines, a military source in the Fifth Infantry Division in Obeid told Mada Masr. *** RSF, SPLM-N press ahead with attacks on Blue Nile’s Kurmuk axis, military takes two areas in Geisan Blue Nile’s Kurmuk locality has entered a second week of attacks by the RSF and SPLM-N forces led by Joseph Tuka, as the allies seek to advance from their positions toward military bases defending the state capital of Damazin. Later in the week, the military mounted a surprise attack in the neighboring Geisan locality, taking two strategic areas that bolster its position on the eastern axis and could put RSF supply lines into the Wad al-Mahi areas they have recently seized at risk, according to a former military officer. The latest round of fighting on the Kurmuk axis began on Monday at Baraka, a strategic military position 12 km northwest of the RSF-held town of Kurmuk. The RSF and SPLM-N forces set out from the town with dozens of combat vehicles and motorcycles, a military source told Mada Masr. The attacking forces initially broke into Baraka, but the military regrouped and retook its positions, leading to fierce clashes that lasted all day and continued into Tuesday, the source said. The two sides offered conflicting accounts of the outcome. The military’s Fourth Infantry Division in Damazin said on Monday that it repelled the attack, while the RSF announced on Tuesday that it took control of the position. The situation on the ground remains unresolved, however, with both sides still present in the area and its outskirts, a second military source said. The source expected further decisive fighting in the coming days. Baraka lies around 155 km from Damazin and is key to controlling southern Blue Nile. The military withdrew there in large numbers after losing Kurmuk to the RSF for a second time in mid-August. The fighting spread to another key position on Tuesday, when the RSF and SPLM-N attacked Sali, which the military uses as a forward command post for operations in southern Blue Nile. The allies opened with heavy artillery shelling and drone strikes before ground troops advanced from Sarkam, southeast of Sali, the first military source said. The attackers attempted to approach from two directions to encircle the position, with RSF units advancing from the southeast and Tuka’s forces from the south. Tuka’s fighters, however, failed to advance quickly enough to complete the maneuver, the source said. Military reconnaissance aircraft had been tracking the advancing forces, allowing the military to exploit the delay and draw them into an ambush that killed more than 50 fighters, the source said. The military then searched the surrounding area and reinforced security positions around Sali, he added. A former military officer said the attacks on Baraka and Sali form part of the RSF’s broader effort to increase pressure on Damazin. The military recognizes the strategic importance of both positions and is likely to use all available means to secure and defend them, he said. On the Geisan front, the military launched a surprise assault at dawn on Thursday against RSF-held Bakori and Aklili . Advancing from the north and east, its forces had taken full control of both areas by 10 am, seizing five combat vehicles and destroying others. The remaining RSF fighters in the area fled south toward the town of Geisan , a third military source told Mada Masr. The military later said it shot down a strategic drone near Bakori after tracking its entry into Sudanese airspace from Ethiopia. Bakori, located around 70 km from Damazin, hosts the base of the Fourth Division’s 13th Infantry Brigade, which the RSF captured in August. Its recapture could pave the way for further military advances in eastern Blue Nile, the former military officer told Mada Masr, including toward Khartoum Beleil and the town of Geisan. The gains would also give the military greater room to maneuver along the eastern axis and potentially cut RSF supply lines toward Minza al-Nimr and Jabal al-Namr in Wad al-Mahi locality, where the RSF made its first advances earlier this month, the officer said. *** Tasis health minister leaves for Nairobi over Cabinet push to take control of medical aid RSF-led Tasis government Health Minister Alaa Eddin Nugud inspects the progress of high school exams in Nyala, June 15. Courtesy: Tasis Health Ministry. A fight over who gets to control healthcare resources and drug imports inside the RSF-led Tasis government in western Sudan has been simmering for months. Last week, it boiled over, sending Health Minister Alaa Eddin Nugud to Nairobi in protest. The immediate trigger was a proposal by the Cabinet affairs minister to place international medical aid under the Cabinet’s control, which won Prime Minister Hassan al- Taaishy ’s backing last week. Taaishy is now treading carefully, trying to advance the proposal without pushing another member of the political leadership out of a government that is already sensitive to the cost of defections, officials in Tasis told Mada Masr. The tussle for control over the portfolio is unfolding as health services across RSF-held areas in western Sudan continue to deteriorate . Cities, villages and displacement camps sheltering hundreds of thousands of people face severe shortages. Funding cuts have forced many health centers to stop receiving international support, while the facilities that remain open are struggling to keep running. Many are also being pulled into the war effort, with medical resources and facilities needed for civilian care diverted to treat RSF fighters. Nugud first raised the alarm around six months ago, when he complained of growing interference in his ministry’s affairs by the RSF’s medical department — a body closer to a military medical corps — and influential Tasis officials linked to the group, a Health Ministry official told Mada Masr. At the heart of his objections, the official said, was what Nugud saw as an RSF effort to monopolize access to medicines and health facilities for the benefit of its members, interfering with the ministry’s ability to run the health sector. Nugud threatened to resign, but Tasis officials stepped in to defuse the standoff, and he withdrew his resignation, a Cabinet official told Mada Masr. But the protest came at a cost. The Cabinet official said Nugud subsequently faced tight restrictions on his movements and communications, as Tasis sought to prevent him from speaking to the media or leaving the government. With defections and departures threatening to undermine the administration, its leaders were wary of anything that might further damage its standing with international humanitarian organizations, whose procedural recognition is crucial to its ability to operate. Around two months ago, the dispute took a new turn when Cabinet Affairs Minister Musa Khaddam put forward the proposal centralizing control over international aid for the health sector, the Cabinet official said. Under the proposal, cash grants and in-kind donations would be routed through the Cabinet before reaching government departments, ending the direct arrangements between international organizations and the Health Ministry, the official explained. Beneath the dispute over aid management there is also longer-running tensions over civilian drug imports, a Health Ministry official said. The RSF has traditionally controlled Indian pharmaceutical imports reaching Nyala through South Sudan and Uganda. When Tasis began establishing its own government, oversight of medicines for civilian use was handed to the Health Ministry. Influential RSF figures wanted that control back, along with the distribution contracts and profits that come with it, the official told Mada Masr. The official warned that the new proposal could tip the balance in favor of those seeking to return civilian pharmaceutical imports to RSF control. Giving the Cabinet greater oversight of health resources, the official argued, would weaken the ministry’s position and allow influential RSF-aligned figures to sway the government into handing the imports back to the group. The proposal remained idle until last week, when the government discussed the matter after months of delay and Taaishy voiced support for the plan, the official said. Nugud pushed back, arguing that the plan would encroach on his ministry’s technical and executive remit and put decisions over health resources in the hands of the Cabinet, rather than those responsible for assessing the sector’s needs, a Health Ministry official said. That was the breaking point, according to a source close to Nugud and another close to his family. The minister suddenly went out of contact, prompting fears among his loved ones that he had been detained, the sources said. But he eventually got in touch to say he had arrived in Nairobi, where, they added, he would be safe from detention or restrictions. Both sources said he has continued to maintain political contacts with Tasis officials and members of his ministry. With Nugud out of Nyala but not entirely out of the picture, Taaishy began to move forward. He issued directives to develop mechanisms and guidelines for transferring supervisory powers from the Health Ministry, a Tasis official said. The government is keen to keep Nugud in his post and prevent the dispute from spiraling into a broader crisis, the official said. It is now looking for a formula that would clearly define the responsibilities of the Cabinet and the Health Ministry. Taaishy’s stated aim is to centralize aid management, strengthen oversight and present Tasis to international partners and humanitarian organizations as a government capable of running public services. But shifting supervisory authority to the Cabinet risks limiting the ministry’s ability to assess its own needs and direct resources toward the health sector’s priorities, the alliance official said. The stakes are particularly high in Darfur, where health facilities depend heavily on external supplies and humanitarian assistance. Clear procedures for receiving and distributing aid and ensuring the quality of medicines are essential to keeping services running, the official added. For now, neither the Tasis official nor the Cabinet official has confirmed whether a final agreement was reached, and no binding executive decision has been issued. *** Khartoum seeks UN-backed humanitarian steps to stave off truce pressure Sudan’s military-led government is stepping up efforts to promote its vision for ending the war to Western capitals as pressure builds on it to respond to truce proposals advanced by the Washington-led Quad on Sudan. To ease demands that it commit to a broader settlement, the government is seeking to show it can deliver on humanitarian issues as the war expands and conditions for civilians deteriorate, hoping that progress on aid deliveries and civilian protection would help curb international criticism, former and current Sudanese officials and sources close to Burhan and the TSC told Mada Masr. Over the past week, Burhan sent letters to German Chancellor Friedric Merz and United States President Donald Trump, in what former officials said was an effort to project receptiveness to peace initiatives while holding firm on Khartoum’s demands to end the RSF’s presence. That strategy would allow the government to demonstrate engagement on one front without being drawn into military and political arrangements it rejects, the sources said. Khartoum is looking to the UN to help turn that distinction into a workable negotiating track, and to Western capitals to foot the bill for whatever is agreed upon. Germany is one of the countries Khartoum is courting. Burhan’s letter to Merz was delivered to Berlin by Darfur Governor Minni Arko Minnawi, who met German Foreign Office Minister of State Serap Guler on October 16. Darfur’s centrality to the war and Minnawi’s standing as a key military ally informed his selection, according to a source at the Sudanese Embassy in Germany. The region is the RSF’s main sphere of influence and seat of its parallel administration, and has suffered some of the war’s worst humanitarian crises. Minnawi leads the Sudan Liberation Movement, a major military ally that, alongside the military establishment, has staunchly opposed any truce that would stop short of removing the RSF and its structures from Darfur. According to the source, the government wants Berlin to help rally European support and revive commitments made at the International Conference on Sudan hosted by Germany in April, particularly those that could help fund and implement humanitarian measures through the UN. The effort builds on Burhan’s discussions with the UN secretary general’s Personal Envoy Pekka Haavisto during the latter’s visit to Khartoum in September. The two discussed what a Foreign Ministry official said is referred to now within government circles as “confidence-building measures” — de-escalation, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, unrestricted aid deliveries and the release and exchange of detainees. Sudanese authorities are now developing proposals to put those discussions into practice, with defined timelines and mechanisms for verifying compliance, a source close to Burhan told Mada Masr. These measures represent the area in which Sudan’s leadership believes progress remains possible at this stage, he added. The government wants the UN to monitor implementation directly and help resolve obstacles as they arise, the source said. Each measure would have specific commitments and clearly identified international parties to carry them out, making it possible to measure progress without committing to a comprehensive agreement on a military truce, he added. The outreach to Berlin is intended to help turn that framework into something workable, the embassy source said. Days before the dispatch, German Ambassador to Sudan Philipp Vandel had met Foreign Minister Mohie Eddin Salem in Khartoum on October 12 to discuss bilateral relations, reconstruction and Germany’s contribution to addressing the war’s aftermath. Minnawi gave the government’s public line at a meeting hosted by the Sudanese Embassy in Berlin on October 17 and attended by representatives of research centers, media outlets and humanitarian organizations. He said Khartoum was open to initiatives that respected Sudan’s sovereignty, but warned that a truce that fails to address the RSF’s deployment and armament would not bring lasting peace. A day before Minnawi’s visit to Berlin, Burhan sent a letter to Trump “reaffirming Sudan’s commitment to US peace efforts,” the TSC chair and military chief wrote on X. Burhan said his government is ready “to work in good faith with all parties for a just, lasting peace that safeguards our sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity and our people’s dignity.” The pledge comes amid repeated clashes between Burhan and US Senior Advisor for African and Arab Affairs Massad Boulos over truce proposals advanced by the Quad he leads. Khartoum insists that the RSF withdraw from areas it occupies and disarm before any truce, while Boulos has increasingly urged the warring parties to accept the truce without preconditions. The two sides have also clashed over US efforts at the UN Security Council to extend Darfur’s arms embargo to the rest of Sudan and enforce it against state institutions, a move Khartoum has strongly opposed on the grounds that it would equate the military with a “rebel militia.” The direct appeal to Trump echoes Burhan’s earlier efforts to enlist the US president’s intervention outside Boulos’s negotiating track. In the aftermath of Fasher’s fall late last year, Burhan asked Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to urge Trump to intervene directly. Khartoum is using its letters to Berlin and Washington, alongside contacts with the UN, to present itself as willing to engage with peace efforts in the face of international criticism over the continuing war and deteriorating humanitarian conditions, a former Foreign Ministry official and a former General Intelligence Service official said. At the same time, it is holding firm on its demands regarding the unity of state institutions and the future of the RSF, they added. Sudan’s maneuvers come as international diplomacy over the war remains deadlocked, with a growing number of mediation initiatives, political tracks, truce proposals and humanitarian efforts yet to produce a breakthrough. The UN Security Council’s October 16 open session on Sudan offered the same catalogue of concerns: the growing role of drone warfare, external support to the warring parties and an increasingly dire humanitarian crisis. Members remained divided over expanding sanctions, but expressed broader support for African-led mediation and coordination through the international Quintet. Made up of the AU, UN, Arab League, European Union and IGAD, the Quintet has spent months trying to navigate rival political initiatives without throwing its weight behind any one of them. Its efforts to bridge the gap between Khartoum-sponsored intra-Sudanese dialogue and anti-war coalitions seeking their own political track in recent weeks have yet to prove feasible. The latest attempt to coordinate international efforts came at the Sixth Consultative Meeting on Enhancing Coordination of Peace Initiatives and Efforts in Sudan , held in Geneva on Wednesday. The meeting brings together mediators to coordinate their approaches, with the Quad and Quintet expected to meet with Haavisto on its sidelines. Meanwhile, the annual joint consultative meeting of the UN Security Council and the AU Peace and Security Council is scheduled for Friday. A source at the AU Commission told Mada Masr that the bloc believes it should be possible for urgent humanitarian measures to proceed relatively independently of disputes over security arrangements and the political process, while remaining linked to both within a broader negotiating framework. The proliferation of mediation forums remains a major obstacle to progress, the source added, particularly as Sudanese parties and international partners remain divided over the conditions for a truce and the future of transitional governance. *** Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter here . The post Khartoum courts UN-backed relief to stave off truce pressure; Tasis govt heedful after health minister’s angry exit; Abyei strike tests Juba ties; Drones hit RSF, military’s seats of power; RSF pushes in Kurmuk, military wins Geisan ground first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia have completed ratification of Makkah defence pact: FO
items.description: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have completed the ratification processes for the Makkah defence pact while Turkiye was in the process of doing so, Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said on Friday. Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in August, under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all. The pact has gained significance amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, and Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said earlier this week that Pakistan was providing “whatever support is needed” to defend the kingdom. Prior to that, the FO had emphasised that signing the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and committing military capabilities under it were executive functions under Pakistan’s national laws and Rules of Business and did not necessarily require parliamentary approval. Answering questions after the weekly press briefing, the FO spokesperson said that “matters related to the agreement, its ratification and operationalisation remain under discussion by the three parties”. This included discussions during the Strategic Political and Defence Committee, which recently met on Oct 5, he added. “The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement reflects the shared commitment of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye to strengthening collective defence and cooperation for regional security and stability,” Khan said. He further noted that each country followed its own constitutional and legal procedures to approve and ratify international agreements. “Pakistan and [the] Kingdom of Saudi Arabia have already completed their ratification processes, while Turkiye is undertaking the requisite procedures in accordance with its domestic legal framework,” he said. Turkiye submitted the Makkah defence pact to its parliament for ratification earlier this week. The spokesperson highlighted Pakistan’s continued commitment to the letter and spirit of the agreement, which he said “is defensive in nature, consistent with the UN Charter, and aimed at promoting regional peace, security and stability”. Answering a follow-up question regarding Article 2 of the pact, which states that an attack on one party would be considered an attack against all parties, Khan stressed again that the agreement was “essentially defensive in nature” and consistent with Article 51 of the UN Charter, which provides the right to self-defence”. “The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement reflects the shared commitment of all three parties, primarily to strengthening collective defence, deterrence, and regional stability,” he said. He added, “It is not directed against any particular country. It provides a framework for collective assistance in the event of external armed aggression against any party.” According to Khan, the “nature and extent” of any such assistance would be determined collectively by the three countries as the situation arose, “following an objective assessment of the circumstances”. To another question, he clarified that there were “no hidden provisions” in the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. “We endorse the text released in the media from the Turkish Parliament. There are no hidden provisions; the agreement is explicit and clear in its provisions and articles,” he said. Regarding the potential invocation of the agreement in response to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, the spokesperson reiterated that “This matter has to be decided by the three partner countries in accordance with the agreement.” He also expressed Pakistan’s concern over the recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and its implications for regional peace and security. “Our position has been clear and consistent,” Khan said. “We support Yemen’s sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity, and believe that a lasting solution to the conflict can only be achieved through dialogue and a negotiated political settlement … At the same time, we unequivocally condemn attacks against Saudi Arabia and reaffirm our commitment to the Kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, and security.” He stressed that Pakistan remained supportive of any meaningful diplomatic engagement that could contribute to “ending hostilities and achieving a durable political settlement”. Earlier this month, the FO said that Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye had agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom, following an emergency meeting of the SPDC formed under their joint defence agreement in Riyadh. While the statement did not specifically name any threat, the development came against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in the Yemen conflict. The foes have traded strikes since the Houthis seized all of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and took control of the Bab al-Mandab strait in a lightning offensive in September.

items.title: Ga Mantse King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II to chair GJA 30th anniversary Awards
items.description: The Ga Mantse, His Royal Majesty King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, has accepted an invitation to chair the Ghana Journalists Association’s (GJA) 30th anniversary celebration and Awards. The traditional ruler announced his decision during a courtesy visit by the GJA leadership, led by its President, Albert Kwabena Dwumfour. “I gladly accept to chair the GJA Awards and I’m happy to do it with my big brother, Otumfuo Osei Tutu,” he said. The acceptance adds to preparations for the association’s 30th anniversary celebration, which will bring together stakeholders in the media industry to recognise excellence in journalism and the contributions of journalists to national development. Dwumfour highlights media’s influence During the visit, Mr Dwumfour highlighted the media’s influence on national development, stressing that journalism can have far-reaching consequences depending on how it is practised. “It can make or break this country. You would see how the media has been used in several nations. But I believe that in Ghana, we have been progressive under your tenure,” he said. His remarks underscored the importance of responsible journalism and the role of the media in shaping public discourse, promoting accountability and contributing to national progress. The courtesy visit also provided an opportunity for the GJA leadership to engage the Ga Mantse on issues concerning the media and strengthen ties with the traditional institution. The 30th anniversary celebration and Awards form part of the GJA’s efforts to honour journalists whose work has contributed to public education, accountability and national development.

items.title: 24-hour economy foundations laid, jobs next – Ricketts-Hagan
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Cape Coast South and a member of Parliament’s Finance Committee, George Kweku Ricketts-Hagan, says the government’s next priority under the 24-hour economy policy is to translate the groundwork already laid into sustainable jobs, particularly for the country’s growing youth population. He said the policy’s initial foundations had been established, but its success would depend on the effective implementation of measures to stimulate economic activity and expand employment opportunities. Speaking to the Ghana News Agency on the sidelines of the recently concluded International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group annual meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, Mr Ricketts-Hagan, who is also Board Chairman of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) and a former Deputy Finance Minister, said economic stabilisation must now be accompanied by job creation. Launched in July 2025, the 24-hour economy policy is designed to boost productivity, promote industrialisation, strengthen export-led growth and create jobs by encouraging businesses to operate beyond conventional working hours. Ricketts-Hagan described the initiative as a long-term undertaking that requires careful planning, noting that the 24-hour Economy Secretariat had established the necessary foundations for implementation. “We probably did not comprehend the enormity of the initiative, but it’s not something that’s supposed to be short-term. It’s long-term, so it has to be planned properly. What the 24-hour Economy Secretariat has done is that they’ve put the building blocks in,” he said. His comments come amid concerns from some economic watchers about the proposed three-shift system, a key component of the policy, with calls for a phased implementation approach backed by annual budgetary allocations.Breaking News Alerts Ricketts-Hagan said the next stage must focus on building on the existing groundwork to deliver the policy’s employment and economic growth objectives. He identified reliable electricity supply, incentives for businesses and access to ready markets for goods and services as critical conditions for the initiative to succeed. According to him, tax reductions could encourage businesses to extend their operating hours, but such incentives would have limited impact without a dependable power supply to support continuous production. On broader efforts to tackle unemployment, particularly among young people, Mr Ricketts-Hagan expressed optimism about the proposed US$10 billion New Economy policy, which is expected to be introduced in 2027. He said the framework would build on existing economic reforms and direct government spending towards sectors with the potential to drive targeted growth and generate sustainable employment. “I do not want to pre-empt the Finance Minister, but the New Economy will build on existing reforms and focus on growing the economy in a manner that creates sustainable employment,” he said.

items.title: Burkina Faso : Abdramane Guinko offre plus d’un million de F CFA de vivres à l’ASVOVIG
items.description: Le vendredi 23 octobre 2026, Abdramane Guinko, un Burkinabè résidant aux États-Unis, a offert un don de vivres à l’Agence de soutien aux veuves, orphelins et victimes de guerre (ASVOVIG). D’une valeur de 1 million de F CFA , ce don est composé de riz, de spaghettis et d’huile. Il vise à soutenir les personnes touchées par les conséquences de la guerre et s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’appel à la solidarité lancé par les autorités burkinabè. À travers ce geste, Abdramane Guinko entend apporter son soutien aux veuves, aux orphelins et aux victimes de guerre. Cette initiative traduit également sa volonté de contribuer à l’élan de solidarité nationale en faveur des personnes affectées par la crise sécuritaire. Burkinabè résidant aux États-Unis, le donateur souhaite, par ailleurs, encourager ses compatriotes, où qu’ils se trouvent, à suivre son exemple. Il les invite à contribuer à cet effort de solidarité nationale et à soutenir les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), ainsi que les populations touchées par la guerre. Recevant le don, le directeur général de l’ASVOVIG, le Colonel-médecin Lamine Ouédraogo, a salué cette initiative. S’adressant au donateur, il a souligné que la solidarité envers son pays ne dépend pas du lieu de résidence. « Vous symbolisez le fait qu’être Burkinabè ne signifie pas seulement être sur le territoire burkinabè. Être Burkinabè va au-delà de cela » , a-t-il déclaré. Le directeur général a également exprimé sa reconnaissance à Abdramane Guinko pour son geste et son engagement en faveur des personnes vulnérables. Il a souligné l’importance de cet élan de solidarité dans l’accompagnement des actions menées par l’ASVOVIG. En reconnaissance de sa contribution, Abdramane Guinko a reçu une attestation de reconnaissance de la part de l’agence. Au-delà de sa valeur matérielle, ce don illustre l’engagement d’un Burkinabè de la diaspora envers son pays et ses compatriotes éprouvés par la guerre. Il rappelle que la solidarité nationale peut s’exprimer au-delà des frontières et que chaque contribution compte dans le soutien aux personnes vulnérables. Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Abdramane Guinko offre plus d’un million de F CFA de vivres à l’ASVOVIG est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Un « programme Captain America pour chiens » : au Texas, une start-up veut modifier génétiquement les auxiliaires canins de l’armée américaine
items.description: Warhound, une nouvelle start-up américaine créée par le cofondateur d’Anduril, Palmer Luckey, et Ben Lamm, à la tête de Colossal Biosciences, une entreprise de biotechnologie qui veut faire renaître des espèces disparues, comme le mammouth laineux, a obtenu 200 millions de dollars de financement pour cloner et modifier génétiquement des « chiens de guerre » destinés à l’armée et aux forces de l’ordre américaines Warhound raises $200M to engineer war dogs and arm them with Anduril gear », TechCrunch , 22 octobre 2026.'> 1 . L’entreprise sera dirigée par David Spirk, un vétéran du corps des Marines, ancien premier directeur des données du Pentagone et conseiller chez Palantir, l’entreprise de surveillance cofondée par Peter Thiel. Warhound revendique être « certifiée par l’American Humane Society », une organisation américaine dédiée au bien-être animal, et qu’elle permettra à terme de limiter le nombre de chiens soumis à un entraînement intensif inutile What is Warhound, Palmer Luckey's war dog startup that just emerged from stealth ? », Business Insider , 23 octobre 2026.'> 2 . En février, l’inspection générale du Pentagone avait pointé du doigt dans un rapport les mauvaises conditions d’hébergement des chiens militaires dans les chenils de douze bases du pays, liées à la mort de quatre d’entre eux entre 2021 et 2023. Vidéo mise en ligne sur le site de Warhound. La création de Warhound repose sur un constat : plus de 80 % des chiens de l’armée américaine sont importés d’Europe, selon l'entreprise, et moins de la moitié sont jugés aptes au service. Or, ces animaux sont encore utilisés à large échelle pour des missions de détection d’explosifs, de recherche ou d’autres tâches jugées trop dangereuses pour les humains ou trop difficiles pour les machines. Warhound prévoit ainsi de sélectionner les chiens considérés comme les plus performants, de conserver leurs cellules dans une biobanque puis de les cloner. Leurs gènes seront ensuite modifiés afin d’accroître leur longévité et d’améliorer leur santé et leurs performances. Sur son site, la start-up, installée au Texas, vante « une nouvelle race de domination […] construite pour la victoire ». Luckey évoquait déjà en 2023 la possibilité de modifier génétiquement des chiens pour les besoins de l’armée. Dans un épisode de podcast auquel participait notamment Jacob Helberg, nommé sous-secrétaire d’État aux affaires économiques par Trump en janvier 2025, Luckey déclarait : « Vous pensez que des bergers allemands de 70 kilos font de bonnes unités canines ? Et des loups sinistres ( « direwolves » ) de 270 kilos qui portent 70 kilos d’armure ? […] Ils sont éteints pour le moment, mais ils ne doivent pas nécessairement le rester ». Anduril Founder @PalmerLuckey spoke about this in 2023 : “You could give every canine unit the characteristics of the strongest Arctic Wolf that ever walked the earth.” “How about Dire Wolves ? 600-pound canines units carrying 150 pounds of armor.” pic.twitter.com/KGqyzBtJQO https://t.co/BsbQPq6pWb — Jawwwn (@jawwwn_) October 22, 2026 En plus de modifier le patrimoine génétique des chiens afin de les rendre plus performants et plus résistants, Warhound affirme vouloir les équiper de technologies de pointe, produites par Anduril, afin de leur fournir une « conscience situationnelle sur le champ de bataille ». Ben Lamm le résume ainsi : il s’agit d’un « programme Captain America pour les chiens » Palmer Luckey unveils start-up to breed ‘genetically enhanced’ dogs for military », Financial Times , 23 octobre 2026.'> 3 . L’article Un « programme Captain America pour chiens » : au Texas, une start-up veut modifier génétiquement les auxiliaires canins de l’armée américaine est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: SIAO 2026 : Plus de 6 000 exposants et une trentaine de pays attendus
items.description: À l’approche de la 18e édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), prévue du 30 octobre au 8 novembre 2026, le comité d’organisation a animé une conférence de presse, le vendredi 23 octobre 2026, sur le site du SIAO à Ouagadougou. Objectif : dresser l’état d’avancement des préparatifs. « Artisanat africain et industrialisation : quelle synergie pour une meilleure organisation et valorisation des produits locaux et du patrimoine culturel ? », tel est le thème retenu pour cette 18e édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO). Le Presidium… À une semaine de l’ouverture, le comité d’organisation a dévoilé les principales innovations de cette édition. Parmi celles-ci figurent la tenue d’ateliers thématiques destinés à mieux vulgariser les métiers de l’artisanat au Village artisanal de Ouagadougou (VAO), la création d’un nouvel espace baptisé « Village du pays invité d’honneur », l’augmentation du nombre de portes d’entrée et de sortie du site, ainsi que l’organisation d’activités sportives. Le Ghana est le pays invité d’honneur de cette 18e édition, placée sous le très haut patronage du président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Plus de 6 000 exposants et une trentaine de pays attendus. Minute.bf

items.title: Innovation, financement et résilience climatique: l’État engage des réflexions sur le logement
items.description: Dakar abrite depuis hier, jeudi 22 octobre, le Salon international de l’habitat, du logement et de la construction au Sénégal, qui porte sur le thème : « L’habitat souverain : Sunu dekkuwaay ». Cette rencontre de trois jours a pour but de créer des ponts entre acteurs du secteur de l’habitat afin de promouvoir un accès au logement décent et durable et un développement urbain mieux maîtrisé. Placé sous le thème : « L’habitat souverain : Sunu dekkuwaay », le Salon international de l’habitat, du logement et de la construction au Sénégal s’est ouvert hier, jeudi 22 octobre, à Dakar, pour trois jours d'échanges et de partenariat. L'objectif de cette édition est de promouvoir des solutions adaptées aux réalités locales fondées sur le transfert de compétences, la planification urbaine, l'innovation, le financement adapté et la résilience climatique. Selon Moussa Bala Fofana, ministre de l’Urbanisme, des Collectivités territoriales et de l’Aménagement du territoire, l’habitat est une condition fondamentale de la dignité humaine, un droit social inaliénable. Pour lui, « à Dakar, plus d'un ménage sur deux est locataire et le poids écrasant des loyers étouffe les budgets des familles ». Poursuivant, il a rappelé que les inondations récurrentes, la précarité des quartiers sous-équipés et la tragédie dramatique des effondrements d’immeubles « sont les symptômes d’une urbanisation anarchique et non maîtrisée dans nos villes ». Cependant, le ministre estime qu’une ville doit naître d'une vision stratégique, d'un aménagement préalable et d'investissements cohérents. Les citoyens doivent accéder au logement abordable via l'achat direct, la location-vente ou la location encadrée. Dans cette perspective, Moussa Bala Fofana a fait savoir que dans chaque projet agréé, l’État exige un équilibre républicain de 50 % de logements sociaux et abordables et de 50 % de logements libres, garantissant à la fois la solidarité sociale et la rentabilité économique des investisseurs. Astou Rose Gaye, directrice générale de la Banque de l’habitat du Sénégal (Bhs), pense que l’accès à un logement décent ne doit pas être un privilège. À l’heure actuelle, dit-elle, le Sénégal doit produire des habitations qui répondent aux attentes légitimes des Sénégalais tout en restant compatibles avec leur pouvoir d'achat. Un conseil interministériel sur le logement prévu Selon Moussa Bala Fofana, il est prévu, en fin octobre, la tenue d’un conseil interministériel sur le logement, l’organisation de la table ronde des bailleurs et investisseurs au début du mois de novembre 2026 et la pose de la première pierre de la nouvelle Ville de Thiès en mi-décembre 2026. Le ministre de l’Urbanisme, des Collectivités territoriales et de l’Aménagement du territoire a aussi annoncé qu’à Dakar, Pikine, Guédiawaye, Thiès et Saint-Louis, le plan de restructuration urbaine cible 300 hectares pour générer 45.000 logements décents, soutenus par un investissement prévisionnel de 1100 milliards de FCfa sur 15 ans. Face à la menace des édifices dégradés, l’État, informe-t-il, a lancé le Plan national de traitement des bâtiments menaçant ruine. D’après lui, un audit identifie 14.000 constructions à diagnostiquer à l'échelle nationale. Pour le ministre, « rien qu’à Dakar, notamment à la Médina, Colobane, Biscuiterie et Grand Dakar, une première tranche d’urgence de 14 opérations prioritaires pour 24,6 milliards de FCfa est engagée dans le but de reconstruire et reloger en toute sécurité ». Pour résorber le déficit national, estimé à 500.000 logements, la feuille de route, indique M. Fofana, vise la production annuelle régulière de 33.000 logements, injectant ainsi près de 800 milliards de FCfa par an dans l'économie nationale. Bada MBATHIE

items.title: Lutte contre la Diphtérie : Kédougou renforce la riposte contre l’épidémie
items.description: Un projet d’urgence de 60 jours a été lancé hier à Kédougou pour renforcer la vaccination, sensibiliser les populations et améliorer la détection précoce des cas de diphtérie. Soutenue par le fonds Start Network, cette initiative vient en appui aux actions déjà engagées par l’État. Présidant la rencontre de lancement, le préfet de Kédougou, El Hadji Malick Sémou Diouf, a souligné l’importance de la mobilisation des acteurs et des communautés pour freiner la propagation de la maladie, dont des cas ont été confirmés dans la région depuis août. Il a également invité les populations à se rapprocher rapidement des structures sanitaires en cas de signes suspects. Mis en œuvre par Kédougou Encadrement et Orientation du Développement Humain (KEOH), en collaboration avec les autorités sanitaires, le projet couvre cinq régions du Sénégal, dont Kédougou, Dakar, Louga, Thiès et Diourbel. Selon Djaliba Tandian, manager de KEOH, l’intervention vise à combler les insuffisances de moyens et à soutenir les activités prévues par les services sanitaires. Une centaine de relais communautaires seront ainsi identifiés, formés et accompagnés pour intensifier la sensibilisation. Le projet prévoit également un appui aux équipes mobiles de vaccination afin de vérifier le statut vaccinal des enfants et de compléter les doses manquantes, y compris pour ceux qui ne sont pas encore vaccinés. L’objectif est de renforcer la prévention et de contribuer à enrayer la propagation de la diphtérie. Amadou DIOP (Correspondant)

items.title: «Haute trahison» : Mariani réagit sur RT à l’alliance de Kabila avec le M23 en RDC
items.description: Le 12 octobre, a Goma, le Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN) a devoile sa direction. Joseph Kabila, president de la Republique democratique du Congo (RDC) entre 2001 et 2019, en prend la tete. Dans les rangs de ce nouveau mouvement figurent Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa et Sultani Makenga, trois responsables associes a l'AFC/M23. Ce dernier controle Goma et mene des combats contre l'armee congolaise. Presente comme une alternative au pouvoir de Kinshasa, le FRN associe ainsi l'ancien chef d'etat a des figures de la rebellion. C'est sur cette alliance que RT a interroge Thierry Mariani. Une comparaison avec Charles de Gaulle Mariani precise que le jugement sur l'ancien president revient d'abord aux Congolais. « Je dis simplement que, quand je vois l'attitude de M. Kabila, je pense que c'est aux Congolais de le juger », a-t-il explique. Il a ensuite rapproche la situation de l'histoire de France. « Est-ce que vous imaginez, pendant la Deuxieme Guerre mondiale, le general de Gaulle s'allier avec l'Allemagne nazie qui occupait une partie du territoire de la France pour prendre le pouvoir en France ? », a demande l'eurodepute. « ecoutez, si c'etait en France, on appellerait ca une haute trahison, et ca merite le châtiment qu'on connaît » , a-t-il declare. Pour Mariani, un dirigeant qui s'associe a un mouvement occupant une partie de son pays ne peut se presenter comme son liberateur. Les relations entre Paris et Kigali evoquees Mariani a egalement ete interroge sur la reaction des capitales europeennes a la situation dans l'est de la RDC. Il attribue leur retenue a la place qu'occupe encore le genocide de 1994 dans les relations avec le Rwanda. « Et comme cette rente memorielle, pour reprendre une expression de M. Macron, est la, les Occidentaux, les Europeens n'osent pas reagir », a-t-il affirme. L'eurodepute a ensuite parle des rencontres entre Emmanuel Macron et Paul Kagame. « Regardez ce qui se passe. M. Macron a recu de multiples fois M. Kagame a l'elysee, c'est meme l'un de ses presque plus proches amis en Afrique, et il ne fait rien », a-t-il declare. Mariani considere que les relations politiques avec Kigali influencent la reponse europeenne aux evenements dans l'est congolais. Son entretien a RT intervient alors que la creation du FRN a replace le role de Joseph Kabila et les rapports avec le Rwanda dans le debat politique en RDC.

items.title: Le sommet Corée du Nord–États-Unis de 2026 : que négocier et que préserver ?
items.description: À télécharger Lire la note (PDF) L’un des principaux facteurs susceptibles de déterminer l’évolution de la péninsule coréenne au second semestre 2026 est la volonté de plus en plus ouvertement affichée par le président américain Donald Trump de renouer avec la diplomatie des sommets avec Kim Jong-un, président de la Commission des affaires d’État de la Corée du Nord. Le 16 août, en ordonnant une réduction substantielle des exercices militaires conjoints entre la Corée du Sud et les États-Unis, Donald Trump a directement évoqué sa « très bonne relation » avec Kim Jong-un ; trois jours plus tard, il a publiquement déclaré vouloir le rencontrer avant la fin de l’année. Ces déclarations dépassent le registre de la simple rhétorique : elles montrent que la Maison-Blanche a inscrit la possibilité d’un sommet à son agenda diplomatique concret.
